docs.title: LaserIO
docs.text:
Guide by: Elon-chan

LaserIO is a powerful, early game, logistic mod. It is capable of moving items, fluids, energy and redstone signals wirelessly, at decently high rates.

It is only gated by the acquisition of Gold, most of it's parts requiring Gold Nuggets. Gold can be acquired early game from Copper and Magnetite (obtainable from Sieving Gravel) by using Bulk Washing from Create or Centrifugation from Create:Vintage.

If you prefer a video guide on LaserIO, direwolf20 has a full guide with timestamps on YouTube: - Mod Spotlight LaserIO - by direwolf20

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
To start, you will want to make a few Logic Chips by smelting Raw Logic Chips. Those are used in everything LaserIO related, so you will want a good supply of them.

The first thing you will want to craft is a Laser Wrench.

docs.title: Quick Example Setup
docs.text:
If you don't care to learn all the intricacies of LaserIO, here is a quick tutorial on how to move Cobblestone from an Igneous Extruder to a Drawer.

  • Step 1 - Place one Laser Node on the Igneous Extruder and one on the Drawer. The side you place the Nodes on doesn't matter, in this case we are using the top.

  • Step 2 - Open the Laser Node above the Igneous Extruder, making sure you are on the correct side tab. The tabs on top will show the block the specific face is pointing at, open the one that shows the Igneous Extruder (down in our case) and place an Item Card inside.

  • Step 3 - R-Click the Item Card inside the Node UI to open the config screen. Use the top-left-most button to switch the card to Extract mode.

  • Step 4 - Now go to the Laser Node above the Drawer (make sure to select the correct side the same way as with the Igneous Extruder) and place an Item Card inside. This will not need to be configured as Cards are Insert mode by default.

  • Step 5 - Take your Laser Wrench and Sneak + R-Click one of the Nodes. It will turn green to show that it is selected. Then head over to the other Node and R-Click it. You will see a red line form between the Nodes. Some particle effects will appear on the Card connections above the blocks when items get moved.

Congratulations! You now have a simple LaserIO system that moves Cobblestone from an Igneous Extruder into a Drawer.

Alternatively, you could do it with a single Laser Node by placing both the Igneous Extruder and the Drawer next to the same Node, since all sides work individually.

Speed

If you want to speed things up, you can place Logistic Overclockers inside the Extract Card (the one on the Igneous Extruder) to make it work faster.

This guide should allow you to understand the mod at a basic level. If you need additional info or you are curious about some of the advanced features of the mod, you can check the other pages on LaserIO.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
There are four types of Logistic Cards in LaserIO, each with their own use.

Card Types

Item Card Fluid Card Energy Card Redstone Card

The Item Card is used to move Items in and out of various inventories, as well as being able to scan inventories for certain items in order to output a redstone signal.

The Fluid Card is used to move fluids in and out of various inventories, as well as being able to scan inventories for certain fluids in order to output a redstone signal.

The Energy Card is used to move energy in and out of various machines and other energy blocks, as well as being able to read the energy level in order to output a redstone signal.

The Redstone Card is a bit more special than the others. It is able to read and transmit redstone signals as well as perform logic operations on those same signals before outputting them. It is also necessary for redstone control on the other Cards.

docs.title: Logistic Overclocker
docs.text:
The Item and Fluid Cards have limits on how much they can move in a single operation and how often they operate. Logistic Overclockers can be used to increase the amount moved in one operation and decrease the time between operations.

You can have up to 4 in a Card and they only affect the Extract, Stock and Sensor modes. The Insert mode is unaffected because it is passive.

docs.title: Configuration & UI
docs.text:
You can configure a card by either pressing R-Click with it in hard, or by pressing R-Click on the Card inside the Laser Node UI.

Tip

If you want to return a Card to its default, non-configured state, you can put it inside a crafting grid, which will remove all NBT data from the Card. Filters will also be extracted and left inside the crafting grid.

Although, Cards are so cheap that you generally just trash them and make new ones instead.

docs.title: Common UI Elements
docs.text:
Those elements mostly apply to Item, Fluid and Energy Cards, due to their similarity, but the Redstone Card shares some features as well, mainly the Card Mode and Channel functionality.

The Redstone Card is covered more in depth in its own section further down.

  1. Card Mode - Switches between Insert, Extract, Stock and Sensor for Item/Fluid/Energy Cards. Switches between Input and Output for Redstone Cards.

  2. Directional Config (Sneaky Mode) - By default, the Card will interact with the side of the block it is pointing at, but it can be changed to any side. For example, you can interact with the bottom of a Furnace even if the Laser Node is on top. Useful for blocks that have sided configs.

  3. Filter Slot - Only available for the Item and Fluid Cards. Allows the use of various Filters. The Counting Filter in particular has slightly different functionality based on mode.

  4. Redstone Mode - Can be used to control the activity of the Card by using a Redstone Channel. By default it is Ignored (meaning Off).

  5. Redstone Channel - Does nothing unless combined with Redstone Mode. Read the previous item.

  6. Logistic Overclock Slot - Special slot for putting in Logistic Overclockers. Only available for Item and Fluid Cards.

  7. Channel - You can group together cards by Channel (NOT the same thing as Redstone Channel!!!). Cards from different channels will not interact even if on the same network.

Energy Card

As you can see, the Energy Card is very similar to the Item and Fluid Cards.

It differs a bit because it cannot be Overclocked or filtered.

Instead of the Filter it gets an Energy Limit setting which can be used to set a percentage that controls the card based on how full (of energy) is the target. It does different things based on the mode. Can be adjusted by clicking.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
You can switch between modes with the top-left most button.

Info

  • The Item and Fluid Cards share the same operation modes and configs so they will be covered together.
  • The Energy Card is slightly different from the last two, but still very similar so it will receive special mention only where necessary.
  • The Redstone Card is completely different and has its own section.

docs.title: Item/Fluid/Energy Cards
docs.text:
Insert, Extract, Stock and Sensor modes for the Item, Fluid and Energy Cards:

Card Modes

InsertExtractStockSensor

Since Insert Cards are passive, the functionality of the Insert mode changes based on how other Cards on the network interact with them.

  • Extract - Pushes into Insert Cards.
  • Stock - Pulls from Insert Cards.
Item / Fluid Energy
  1. Priority - If multiple cards on the network can be used at the same time, which one to pick. Higher Priority means it gets to go first.

Energy Limit

For Insertion, the Energy Limit setting on the Energy Card dictates how much it should fill the target when inputting energy from an Extract Card, or how much to drain the target when pulling energy for a Stocking Card.

Counting Filter

The Counting Filter tells the Insert Card how much to keep inside the target, weather when pushing inside or pulling out.

The Extract Card pulls Items/Fluids/Energy out of the target block.

Item / Fluid Energy

  1. Round Robin - Makes it so it tries to rotate through Insert Cards when pushing stuff. Enforced makes it stop until it can insert into the next card, forcing it to spread equally. Off by default.

  2. Exact Mode - Forces it to wait until it can do a full Transfer Amount or a full Counting Filter limit, whichever is smaller. Off by default.

  3. Transfer Amount - How much to try to extract from the target in a single operation. Can be adjusted by clicking. Logistic Overclockers increase the maximum.

  4. Speed (Ticks) - How long to wait between operations (less means it goes faster). Can be adjusted by clicking. Logistic Overclockers decrease the minimum.

Both Transfer Amount and Speed are maxed out by default for Energy Cards.

Energy Limit

For Extraction, the Energy Limit setting on the Energy Card dictates how much it should leave inside the target it's pulling from.

Counting Filter

The Counting Filter tells the Extract Card how much to leave inside the target when pulling.

The Stock Card performs operations using Filters, interacting with Insert Cards on the same network. The exact functionality changes based on configuration.

Item / Fluid Energy

  1. Regulate - Only works with a Counting Filter, otherwise it does nothing. If the number of items/fluids inside the target exceed the Counting Filter limit, they will be pulled out and sent to valid Insert Cards, similar to how an Extract Card would work. Off by default.

  2. Exact - Forces it to wait until it can do a full Transfer Amount or a full Counting Filter limit, whichever is smaller. Off by default.

  3. Transfer Amount - How much to try to extract from the target in a single operation. Can be adjusted by clicking. Logistic Overclockers increase the maximum.

  4. Speed (Ticks) - How long to wait between operations (less means it goes faster). Can be adjusted by clicking. Logistic Overclockers decrease the minimum.

Both Transfer Amount and Speed are maxed out by default for Energy Cards.

Warning

The Stock mode for Item/Fluid Cards NEEDS a filter and only works with a filter in allow mode.

Energy Limit

For Stock, the Energy Limit setting on the Energy Card dictates how much it should fill the target. If the target exceeds the Energy Limit, it will instead start pulling energy and sending it to Insert Cards.

Counting Filter

The Counting Filter tells the Stock Card how much to keep inside the target when pushing. It also has the special interaction with Regulate mentioned before.

The Sensor Card checks the target block and compares it against its filter, generating a redstone signal based on the result.

Item / Fluid Energy

  1. Logic Operation - Wether to perform OR/AND on the filters. Only available on Item/Fluid Cards.

  2. Speed (Ticks) - How long to wait between operations (less means it goes faster). Can be adjusted by clicking. Logistic Overclockers decrease the minimum.

  3. Exact - Untested functionality, unknown what exactly it does. Only available on Energy Cards. Off by default.

Speed is maxed out by default for Energy Cards.

Warning

The Sensor mode for Item/Fluid Cards NEEDS a filter because otherwise it has nothing to check against.

Energy Limit

Untested functionality, unknown what exactly it does.

Redstone Channel

Sensor mode acts more like a Redstone Card. It only features a Redstone Channel option because the output is a redstone signal, which will go to that specific channel.

docs.title: Redstone Cards
docs.text:
The Redstone Card function differently and uniquely compared to the other three.

Card Modes

InputOutput

Reads the redstone level from the target and sends it to the selected Redstone Channel.

Interval OFF Interval ON

  1. Card Mode - Same as with the other three cards, changes between the two modes.

  2. Interval - Checks the redstone level against a lower bound (1st box) and an upper bound (2nd box), outputting the selected strength (3rd box) into the Redstone Channel if the redstone signal from the target block in between the bounds.

  3. Redstone Channel - Replaces the regular Channel from the other three Cards. Used to group together the Cards.

Advanced Comparator

The Input mode can be used as a compact, and more advanced, Comparator by using the Interval. By adjusting the upper and lower bounds you can get it to work as a greater than, smaller than or equal to operator (as well as their combinations).

Outputs the redstone level from the selected Redstone Channel to the target.

Logic OFF Logic ON

  1. Card Mode - Same as with the other three cards, changes between the two modes.

  2. Weak/Strong Signal - What level signal to output. Weak means whatever is coming in, Strong is always 15.

  3. Redstone Channel - Replaces the regular Channel from the other three Cards. Used to group together the Cards.

  4. Redstone Operation - Off by default. Can perform a NOT or Complementary operation on the redstone signal. Complementary means it flips the strength on the 0-15 scale.

  5. Logic Operation - Off by default. If turned on, you have the option to select a second Redstone Channel to perform a logic operation together with. Available operators are: OR, AND, XOR.

By combining the two modes, you can perform quite advanced redstone functions without the need for additional, external tools.

docs.title: Laser Connectors
docs.text:
Connectors have the role of carrying connections across longer distances.

Laser Connectors don't have any function besides connecting to other parts. They have the same connection distance as a Node and are mostly used to traverse longer distances without needing to use Nodes in-between. They act as a sort of "wire pole" for the network.

docs.title: Advanced Laser Connector
docs.text:
There is also an Advanced Laser Connector, which functions somewhat similarly to the normal Laser Connector, with a few key differences.

The Advanced Laser Connectors have no range limit and even work across dimensions. They can only be connected one-to-one, meaning you can't connect one Advanced Laser Connector to more than one other Advanced Laser Connector. They can still connect to as many other Nodes and basic Laser Connectors as you want, but only withing the 8 block range.

When two Advanced Laser Connectors are linked, their laser line will point up (relative to the way it is facing) into a small, dark cube. If looking at a linked Advanced Laser Connector while holding the Laser Wrench, you will be able see the coordinates of the other Advanced Laser Connector near the center of the screen.

docs.title: Laser Node
docs.text: Laser Nodes are the main part of a LaserIO network. They connect to other Nodes and Connectors, sharing this functionality with Laser Connectors, while also being able to perform all the logistic functions via Cards.

docs.title: Node UI
docs.text:
If you open a Laser Node, you will be greeted with this UI:

  1. Card Inventory Grid - Where you will place your Cards.

  2. Network Settings - A tab for customizing the colors of the laser network the node is part of. It will change the colors of the entire network at once. Purely visual, has no practical function.

  3. Show Particles - Toggle the particle effects that happen when a Card does something. Purely visual but it can cause lag if theres too many, so turning them off may be preferred.

  4. Node Overclocker Slot - Special slot for putting in Node Overclockers.

  5. Side Tabs - Each side of a Laser Node has it's own Card Inventory Grid, with the tabs at the top letting you switch between all of them without needing to open the exact face in world.

docs.title: Node Overclocker
docs.text:
For any side of a Laser Node, only one card can run at a time. If you have multiple Cards per side, you will want to use Node Overclock Cards.

You can add up to 8 Node Overclocks to a Node, each additional card allowing one more Card to function in parallel. The Node Overclock Cards are shared across all the sides of the Laser Node.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text: Filters are used inside the filter slot of Cards, which is only available to Item and Fluid Cards. There are five types: Basic, Counting, Tag, Mod and NBT.

docs.title: Configuring Filters
docs.text:
You can configure a Filter by either pressing R-Click with it in hand, or by placing it inside a Card, which will open the Filter UI in the middle of the Card UI for the Basic, Counting and Mod Filters. For the Tag and NBT Filters, you can open their UI by pressing R-Click on them in the Card UI, which will open their dedicated config UI (this can be done with the first three as well, but isn't needed).

Tip

If you want to wipe the data from any Filter, you can put it inside a crafting grid, which will remove all NBT data from it.

Although, Filters are so cheap you generally just trash them and make new ones instead.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Filter Types

Basic Filter Counting Filter Tag Filter Mod Filter NBT Filter

The Basic Filter allows the filtering of specific items and fluids by placing them in its grid.

You can add items/fluids from your inventory, or drag them from the EMI tab. Fluids are added as their bucket variant, but they work as the fluid inside Fluid Cards.

Top left option buttons:

  • Allow/Deny - Whitelist or Blacklist mode. Allow by default.

  • Match NBT - Whether to check the NBT as well when matching Items/Fluids. Off by default.

The Counting Filter has the same functionality as the Basic Filter, allowing the filtering of specific items and fluids, but also has the ability to set specific amounts. The exact effect the Counting Filter changes based on the mode of the Card and is outlined on the Cards page.

You can add items/fluids from your inventory, or drag them from the EMI tab. Fluids are added as their bucket variant, but they work as the fluid inside Fluid Cards. You can increase the count by using L-Click and decrease it by using R-Click. If you hold Shift while clicking it will increment by 10, and if you hold Ctrl it will increment by 64.

Top left option buttons:

  • Match NBT - Whether to check the NBT as well when matching Items/Fluids. Off by default.

The Tag Filter allows filtering based on tags. If you would like to view tags without using the Tag Filter, you can press F3 + H to turn on Advanced Tooltips in game. EMI sometimes also shows common tags in the "Usage" screen if you turn the pages all the way to the end.

To add tags, you can write them directly in the black box at the top and press Enter. You can also place something in the top-right slot, it will then display a list of tags specific to that item/fluid.

You can click a tag in the list and then press the green, + (plus) button to add it, it will then switch from blue to grey. You can remove an added filter by selecting it and pressing the red - (minus) button. The large X button is used to wipe all settings, removing all filtered tags.

Top left option buttons:

  • Allow/Deny - Whitelist or Blacklist mode. Allow by default.

The Mod Filter allows filtering based on mod that the item/fluid came from. It works similarly to the Basic Filter, but instead of matching the exact item/fluid, it matches the entire mod that it came from.

For example, simply adding cobblestone would match all of Vanilla Minecraft. Adding anything from GT would match the entirety of GT.

You can add items/fluids from your inventory, or drag them from the EMI tab. Fluids are added as their bucket variant, but they work as the fluid inside Fluid Cards.

Top left option buttons:

  • Allow/Deny - Whitelist or Blacklist mode. Allow by default.

The NBT Filter allows filtering based on the NBT values of the item/fluid (although fluids should never have NBT). This filter is very niche and doesn't see much use due to it lacking in functionality.

For NBT filtering it is advised that you instead look towards Pipez, which has a much better NBT filtering method.

The UI is very similar to that of the Tag Filter and works much the same way. To add NBT, you place something in the top-right slot, it will then display a list of NBT values specific to that item/fluid. You could also write the NBT key in the black box at the top and press Enter to add it, but this is hardly useful.

You can click a key in the NBT list and then press the green + (plus) button to add it, it will then switch from blue to grey. You can remove an added filter by selecting it and pressing the red - (minus) button. The large X button is used to wipe all settings, removing all filtered NBT keys.

When hovering over an NBT key in the list it will also display its value, but this is misleading. It only matches the NBT key, and not it's value, which is wh

Top left option buttons:

  • Allow/Deny - Whitelist or Blacklist mode. Allow by default.

docs.title: Laser Wrench
docs.text: The Laser Wrench is used for setting up connections between LaserIO parts, such as Connectors and Nodes, as well as having a few other minor functions. It is the primary tool you will be using when interacting with the mod. It also has forge:wrench functionality, meaning it can interact with some other mods that use wrenches.

docs.title: How to use the Laser Wrench
docs.text:
To use the Laser Wrench you need to Sneak + R-Click a Node or Connector (it will turn green to show it is selected) and then R-Click another Node or Connector to connect them. A line will appear between them to show that they are linked.

One part can be connected to as many other parts as you want, provided they are all within range.

The maximum connection range is 8 blocks, including the parts themselves, meaning there can be at most 6 blocks between any two parts. This range is a sphere and not a cube, so it will be shorter when going diagonally.

Fast Chaining

The Laser Wrench can also be used from the offhand, in which case it will auto-select the last placed Node or Connector, including any you place with the wrench in hand, allowing parts to be quickly chained together.

docs.title: Card Holder
docs.text:
The Card Holder is used as a bag for LaserIO related items. This includes: Cards, Filters and Overclockers.

Most notably, it allows Cards to stack up to 64 instead of the usual single item stacks. Although, for Cards and Filters to stack they need to have the same NBT values, meaning they will not stack if they aren't configured the exact same way.

It is generally used to hold freshly crafted items, since those will stack up naturally.

docs.title: How to use the Card Holder
docs.text:
You can open it by pressing R-Click with it in hand.

It will also open inside the Laser Node UI as a side panel if you have it in your inventory, allowing you to pull cards directly out of it and place them inside the Node.

Auto Pulling

You can also Sneak + R-Click with the Card Holder in hand, which will toggle Auto Pulling.

Auto Pulling makes the Card Holder automatically pick up any LaserIO Cards, Filters and Overclockers that enter your inventory, moving them inside itself.

Helpful for keeping your inventory clean while working.

docs.title: Card Cloner
docs.text: The Card Cloner is used to copy the settings of one Card to another. It can also be used to copy the setting and contents of Laser Nodes.

docs.title: How to use the Card Cloner
docs.text:
On Cards On Nodes

When cloning Cards, the Card Cloner only works inside the Laser Node Card Grid.

To copy a Card take the Card Holder in your cursor and L-Click the Card you want to copy from inside the Node Grid. You will hear a "write" sound if it got copied.

To paste the settings, simply R-Click another Card inside the Node Grid with the Card Holder. You will hear an "enchant" sound if it got pasted.

This will copy everything from the Card, including: Modes, Settings and Filters.

Filters & Overclockers

When cloning Cards, the Card Cloner will attempt to insert Logistic Overclockers and Filters, as well as configure the Filters. It will take them from your inventory or the Card Holder and insert them into the Card.

To clone a Node, you must first select one. You can do this by Sneak + R-Click a Laser Node in the world with the Card Cloner. The selected Node will have a light blue overlay and you will hear a "write" sound.

You can then paste the settings/contents of the selected Node on another Laser Node by R-Click it with the Card Cloner. You will hear an "enchant" sound if it got pasted.

When cloning Nodes, there are two modes. You can switch between them by pressing R-Click in the air with the Card Holder.

  1. Node Contents - This mode copies the Card grid inside the Node UI, as well as the Node Overclocker count. This will copy Cards and all of their configs and contents, including Filters and Logistic Overclockers, similar to how it functions on Cards. It will try to pull everything it needs from your inventory or from the Card Holder.

  2. Network Settings - Simply copies the config from the Network Settings (the black gear icon on the right) of the Laser Node. Network Settings are purely visual.

You can check what the Card Cloner currently has copied by holding Ctrl when hovering over it inside your inventory.

You can clear the data of a Card Cloner by Sneak + R-Click with it in the air.

docs.title: Laser IO
docs.text:
Laser IO is a highly recommended option for wireless FE energy transmit, available pre-LV. Each Laser Node connection can transmit up to 1 million FE/tick, more than enough to last you until mid game and Flux Networks.

For more details, visit the Laser IO page.

docs.title: Create Wires
docs.text: Create Wires are an incredibly cheap option for energy transmission, but have very low transfer speed. Create Wires come in different tiers, with transfer speed ranging from 1024 FE/tick for Copper Wires to 8096 FE/tick for Overcharged Diamond Wires. While viable in LV and MV, it is recommended to switch to Laser IO as soon as possible.

docs.title: Pipez
docs.text: Pipez Energy Pipes are technically available as an option, but are strongly recommended against due to their underwhelming transfer rates without upgrades, with Create Wires offering better speeds at a lower cost. The initial transfer rate is 256 FE/tick, but can thankfully be upgraded up to 131072 FE/tick, although the max tier upgrades are only available at EV.

docs.title: P2P Energy
docs.text: Applied Energistics 2's Energy P2P Tunnels are a space-efficient option offering virtually limitless energy transfer rates available late-MV to early-HV. P2P Tunnels come at a cost, however: transferring energy between P2P Tunnels incurs a 5% energy loss, so Flux Networks are generally preferred to P2P Energy after they are unlocked in EV.

docs.title: Flux Networks
docs.text:
Flux Networks are an incredibly powerful wireless energy transfer (and storage) solution available in EV and gated by PTFE. Flux Nodes have exorbitant transfer rates(1) similar to P2P Tunnels, but don't have any additional energy draw, and are thus recommended as the main FE energy transfer option starting from EV until the very endgame.

  1. up to 2^31 - 1, or 2 147 483 647 FE/tick

docs.title: Fluid Cells
docs.text: Thermal's Fluid Cells are one of the earliest options available for automatic fluid transfer, and are a great option for close-range fluid transport. Fluid Cells have a big initial buffer of 32 buckets, and can be configured to automatically input and output fluids through the menu at a sizable max transfer rate of 8 buckets/tick. Thermal upgrades can be used on Fluid Cells, increasing the buffer to 8192 buckets and transfer rate to an astounding 2048 buckets/tick, making them extremely powerful for close-range fluid transport.

docs.title: Laser IO
docs.text:
Laser IO offers easy wireless fluid transfer, available pre-LV and gated by gold. Laser Nodes can be set to transmit fluids through a Fluid Card, with an initial speed of 5 buckets/second that can be upgraded with 4 Logistic Overclockers to transmit 40 buckets/4 ticks, or 10 buckets/tick. Laser IO is generally recommended for mid-long range fluid transfer until other options like Applied Energistics 2 Networks are available.

For more details, visit the Laser IO page.

docs.title: Create Pipes
docs.text:
Create's Mechanical Pumps and Fluid Pipes are by far the cheapest fluid transfer option available early game, only requiring Copper Plates and spare amounts of Andesite Alloy. However, they require rotational force to operate, and don't have a particularly high transfer rate compared to other options. A Mechanical Pump's transfer rate depends on the RPM according to the formula 0.5mB/tick * RPM, up to a maximum of 128mB/tick(1) for 256 RPM.

  1. 2.56 buckets / second.

docs.title: Pipez
docs.text:
Pipez Fluid Pipes and Ultimate Pipes allow for easy close-mid range fluid transfer, and Ultimate Pipes can be used to make compact item/fluid transport setups, though their initial transfer rate is somewhat slow. The base transfer rate for both pipe types is 50mB/tick(1) and can be upgraded up to 10 buckets/tick in EV.

  1. 1 bucket / second.

docs.title: GregTech Machine Covers
docs.text:
Besides just being a crafting material, GregTech's Electric Pumps (as well as Fluid Regulators) can be installed on the sides of GregTech machines as machine covers, allowing them to push/pull fluids from nearby inventories without taking up space. Fluid Regulators offer additional configuration options compared to Electric Pumps, but are otherwise similar. LV Pumps and LV Fluid Regulators transfer 64mB/tick(1) with the higher tiers providing increasingly higher transfer rates up to a maximum of 1048 buckets/tick at UV.

  1. 1.28 buckets / second.

For more details, visit the GregTech Machine Covers page.

docs.title: Applied Energistics 2
docs.text:
Besides item logistics, Applied Energistics 2 ME Networks can also similarly be used for exceptionally powerful multi-fluid transport and storage. ME Networks are available starting from late-MV to early-HV, and are highly recommended to set up as soon as possible.

For more information on AE2, check out the Applied Energistics 2 section on the wiki.

docs.title: Laser IO
docs.text:
Laser IO Nodes are generally recommended as a powerful option for wireless, long-range item transfer available pre-LV and gated by gold. Laser Nodes can be set to transfer items with an Item Card, at an initial speed of 8 items/second. Item Cards can be upgraded with 4 Logistic Overclockers to transfer up to 64 items/tick(1).

  1. 1320 items/second.

For more details, visit the Laser IO page.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
Create offers a variety of cheap and flexible item transfer options, from Chutes to Mechanical Belts to Mechanical Arms. Create methods of item transfer synergize well with Create machinery, making building automated assembly lines with Create fairly simple.

For more details, check out the Create section on the wiki.

docs.title: GregTech Machine Covers
docs.text:
Besides just being a crafting material, GregTech Conveyors and Robot Arms can be installed on the sides of GregTech machines as machine covers, allowing them to push/pull items from nearby inventorires without taking up space. Robot Arms operate at the same speed as Conveyors, but offer additional configuration options. LV Conveyors and LV Robot Arms transfer 8 items/second, with the higher tiers providing increasingly higher transfer rates up to a maximum of 1024 items/second at LuV.

For more details, visit the GregTech Machine Covers page.

docs.title: Pipez
docs.text:
Pipez Item Pipes and Ultimate Pipes allow for simple close-mid range item transfer, with Ultimate Pipes allowing for compact item/fluid transport, though initial transfer rates without upgrades are relatively slow. The base transfer rate for both pipe types is 4 items / second, and can be upgraded to transfer up to 64 items/tick(1) in EV.

  1. 1320 items/second.

docs.title: Modular Routers
docs.text:
While considered a fairly niche option, Modular Routers can be used to transfer items wirelessly with Puller/Sender Modules. Mk2 Puller Modules pull items up to 12 blocks away (or 24 blocks with 12 Range Augments), while Mk2 Sender Modules send items up to 24 blocks away (or 48 blocks with 24 Range Augments). While the base transfer rate is just 1 item/second, Modular Routers can be easily upgraded with 6 Stack Upgrades to transfer 64 items/second.

Getting Blaze Powder in HV unlocks Mk3 Sender Modules that can send items across an unlimited range, and Speed Upgrades that can be used to increase item transfer speed even further up to 640 items/second.

docs.title: Applied Energistics 2
docs.text:
Applied Energistics 2 ME Networks are an extremely powerful and flexible option for managing item transfer and storage in your base, alongside many other uses. ME Networks are available starting from late-MV to early-HV, and are highly recommended to set up as soon as possible.

For more information on AE2, check out the Applied Energistics 2 section on the wiki.

docs.title: Dynamos
docs.text:
Guide by: humanoferth

Dynamos are a type of block added by Thermal that can generate power. They are often used from LV to EV or early IV. There are 3 types of dynamos:

Stirling DynamoCompression DynamoLapidary Dynamo

Stirling Dynamos use furnace fuel as an input. This is the first dynamo that you can use and are a decent choice for an intial power source.

Compression Dynamos take fluid fuels as their input. While these can be better then the singleblock turbines from gregtech, they are difficult to set up early on and you have much better options.

Lapidary Dynamos use gems as an input to generate power. Out of the three dynamo options, these are the best in terms of ease of setup and maximum power output. These are gated by the assembler and require cobalt brass to craft.

I strongly recommend you use lapidary dynamos as your primary power source if you want to use dynamos for power. It is much easier to scale then the other two sources and will last you a long time, at least until you get better power sources like Nitrobenzene. To make the initial power required to get the lapidary dynamo, stirling dynamos are an option, though I advise against trying to scale them since they are highly inefficient. I strongly advise against using the compression dynamo since it requires much more infrastructure and processing then the lapidary dynamo does, and by the time you can get fuel for it easily you'll have other options.

docs.title: Anatomy of a dynamo
docs.text: Dynamos only output power on the red piece protruding out. It won't output power on any other ends. Similarly, you can't input items on the red piece protruding out, although there are ways to get around this with LaserIO.

docs.title: Calculating Fuel Consumption and FE/t
docs.text:
Without augments, dynamos produce 200 FE/t (4000 FE/s). Fuel consumption can be calculated by dividing the total FE produced by one item (Found in EMI) or bucket of fuel by the FE/s your dynamo is currently producing (factoring in augments). For example, a diamond produces a total of 300,000 FE, as found in EMI. Dividing this by 4000 (FE/s produced by a lapidary dynamo with no augments) gives 1 diamond consumed every 75 seconds. Below are a list of augments and how they effect fuel consumption and power production.

Upgrade KitsARC KitsMCI Kits

Upgrade kits scale machines they are in by some scale factor. In dynamos, this means that they multiply power production and fuel consumption by that scale factor. If, for example, a lapidary dynamo is being fueled by diamonds (produces 300,000 RF each) had an EV upgrade kit (48x scale factor), the dynamo would produce 9,600 RF/t (200 RF/t * 48) while consuming a diamond every 1.5625 seconds (300,000 RF / (9,600 RF/t / 20 t/s)). While you can put multiple upgrade kits in a dynamo, only one of the highest tier one will do anything.

Each tier of upgrade kit will have a scale factor 2x larger then the last, starting at 6 in LV, 12 in LV, 24 in HV, and 48 in HEV

Auxillery Reaction Chamber Kits (ARC's) additively increase power output at the cost of a multiplicative increase in fuel energy. Its really important to keep in mind that these effects are compounding. If, for example, a lapidary dynamo is being fueled by diamonds (produces 300,000 RF each) had an EV ARC (.6x fuel energy, +300% power output), the dynamo would produce 800 RF/t (200 RF/t + (300% * 200 RF/t)) and it would consume a diamond every 11.25 seconds ((300,000 RF * .6)/(800 RF/t * 20 t/s)). A dynamo can take multiple ARC's, where fuel energy is multipled, and power output is added for each ARC. If, for example, a lapidary dynamo is being fueled by diamonds (produces 300,000 RF each) had 3 EV ARC's (.216x fuel energy (.6 ^ 3), +900% power output (300 * 3)), the dynamo would produce 2000 RF/t (200 RF/t + (900% * 200 RF/t)) and it would consume a diamond every 1.62 seconds ((300,000 RF * .216)/(2000 RF/t * 20 t/s)).

Each tier of ARC will decrease fuel the fuel energy multiplier by .1 while increasing fuel energy by 100% (except for LV to MV, which increases by 50%) starting at .9x fuel energy and +50% in LV, .8x fuel energy and +100% in MV, .7x fuel energy and +200% in HV, and .6x fuel energy and +300% in EV.

Multi-cycle Injector Kits (MCI's) multaplicatively decrease fuel consumption without affecting power output. If, for example, a lapidary dynamo is being fueled by diamonds (produces 300,000 RF each) had an EV MCI (1.6x fuel energy), the dynamo would produce 200 RF/t and it would consume a diamond every 120 seconds ((300,000 RF * 1.6)/(200 RF/t * 20 t/s)). A dynamo can take multiple MCI's, where fuel energy is multipled for each ARC. If, for example, a lapidary dynamo is being fueled by diamonds (produces 300,000 RF each) had 3 EV ARC's (4.096x fuel energy (1.6 ^ 3)), the dynamo would produce 200 RF/t and it would consume a diamond every 307.2 seconds ((300,000 RF * 4.096)/(2000 RF/t * 20 t/s)).

Each tier of MCI increases the fuel energy multipler by .15 starting at 1.15x in LV, 1.3x in MV, 1.45x in HV, and 1.6x in EV.

MCI's are better than ARC's since you MCI's just gives fuel more energy at no cost. While ARC's output more power, this increase in power also increases the speed at which fuel is consumed on top of the decrease in fuel. Using the numbers above, a lapidary dynamo with three EV ARC's would consume a diamond every 1.62 seconds and produce 2000 RF/t. To do the same with lapidary dynamos with three MCI's (which consume a diamond every 307.2 seconds and produces 200 RF/t), you could put down 10 lapidary dynamos with three MCI's and get the same power output (200 RF/t * 10) while consuming a diamond every 30.72 seconds (307.2 s / 10).

To better quantify this, suppose you were producing 1 diamond per second. Using 3 EV ARC's (as described above) you could at max produce 3,240 FE/t (1 d/s * 1.62 s/d * 2,000 RF/t) while with 3 EV MCI's you could at max produce 61,440 FE/t *(1 d/s * 307.2 s/d * 200 FE/t) given your willing to put down more dynamos.

Optimally, for a dynamo you'll want to have an upgrade kit and three MCI's of the highest tier you can afford in your dynamos. The upgrade kit will increase power output to help reduce dynamo spam while the MCI's will help alleviate the increases in fuel consumption. Using ARC's will just require you to make more fuel much faster due to the compounding effects, which is especially an issue as fuel will later cost energy itself to make.

docs.text:

It uses 2 LV rock crushers, 2 LV forge hammers, and an LV mechanical sieve. This makes sand, which is then pushed into a mechanical sieve that generates gems. All of these gems are pushed into 12 lapidary dynamos with an LV upgrade kit and 3 LV MCI's. Here is a single module:

It is also slightly positive on fuel to ensure no downtime. This setup can be wallshared on its left, right, and back and can be expanded infinitely to the left and right. Here it is quaded:

If everything is scaled to MV, it would be able to handle 18 dynamos and would produce 332.5A of MV. If everything is scaled to HV, it would be able to handle 26 dynamos and would produce 238.75 of HV. docs.title: Multiblock Design Contest submissions
docs.text:
In September 2026 the community was invited to design new multiblocks for Star Technology in a Discord forum contest. Every submission is collected here, one page per entry, grouped by the voltage tier the author targeted. The pages reproduce what the authors posted (summary, mechanics, screenshots, schematics) and link back to the original Discord thread; they are not a statement about what will be added to the pack.

Note

Entries that span several tiers are listed under their lowest tier. Pages marked incomplete had too little material in the post to describe the design fully.

docs.title: Acoustic Entanglement Device (AED)
docs.text:
Submitted by: Lumen (@deyth), unknown user · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier IV Role Resource generation — ordered-catalyst dust production that does not scale with energy Schematic aed.txt Original post Acoustic entanglement device

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The AED produces processed base resources (dusts) in a unique way: it skips the normal processing lines, but its output does not scale with more energy. It is meant as the reward for solving an optional automation challenge, ordered directional catalyst input, which in turn makes resource production and energy generation easier.

The author frames it with a bit of lore: the "void" around the player is actually an ether full of particles, mystical and natural, and the AED uses sound waves to knock those particles out of the air. Every material is "acoustically attuned", though, and must be unattuned before it can be used.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Acoustic attunement. Every material (hyperbole, per the author) has an attunement: a string of up to 6 "directions" that must be zeroed to unattune it. Example given: Copper is [up], Titanium is [up, up, down], Tungsten is [up, up, down, up, up, down].
  • Ordered catalyst input. To generate a dust, a catalyst is inserted into the bus on the matching "speaker" in the attunement's order. Zeroing a long attunement also zeroes its shorter prefixes along the way: in the example, producing one Tungsten dust also yields 4 Copper and 2 Titanium.
  • Speed. Because catalysts must arrive in strict order, the machine is limited to 1 tick per attunement length. The maximum attunement length is dictated by plastic tier.
  • Acoustic reentanglement mode. The machine can also attune items to specific sound frequencies, unlocking new possibilities:
    • an attuned maintenance hatch increases the fuel efficiency of combustion-based generators (reduced vibration losses);
    • attuned turbines can spin faster (reduced vibration).
  • Possible tweaks the author lists: replace the catalyst input with a redstone signal, and generate material attunements randomly on world creation.

Proposed multiblock structures for the Beacon of Lucidity and the Paragon of the Veil. Both controllers already exist in the pack and already have descriptions, but neither has a multiblock structure yet; this submission proposes one for each. Both are described by the author as a Daydream Spire with infinite connections: the Beacon of Lucidity adds infinite range, and the Paragon of the Veil adds infinite cross-dimensional range.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A GregTech-themed alternative for producing Bio-Diesel fuel for Create: Diesel Generators. The multiblock takes in the base ingredients of both the Create Seed Oil recipe and the Create Ethanol recipe and skips straight to outputting Bio-Diesel. The author's intent is to let Create: Diesel Generators scale more effectively and remain a viable power option further into the game, provided the player is willing to spend the resources, while also giving a non-overpowered demonstration of how some multiblocks enable recipe skipping.

  • Features two input hatches, one per combined recipe, to represent the two recipes being merged. The author notes this is entirely optional if it presents too much of a coding challenge.
  • Coil boosting is proposed as a possible option, as long as it does not risk unbalancing the machine.

docs.title: Condensed Horizon Relativistic Oscillation Nucleus for Output Synthesis (C.H.R.O.N.O.S.)
docs.text:
Submitted by: GeneralXHD (@generalxhd) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UIV+ Role Utility — produces a time-manipulating fluid that boosts late-game recipes Schematic chronos.txt Original post C.H.R.O.N.O.S

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
A late-game multiblock aimed at players struggling with the recipe attributes of endgame machines (the author's term for everything that defines how a recipe runs: time, product, educt, parallels, and so on). The CHRONOS condenses time itself around its core into a fluid, Dense Temporal Concentrate (DTC), which certain machines can consume to alter their recipe parameters. The author presents it as a new "boost" system alongside bulking, threading, and parallels, but more limited: because it cannot be spammed, its effects are meant to be stronger than the traditional boosts.

Only one CHRONOS can exist per world.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
The author stresses that everything below is a suggestion and that the numbers, formulas, conversion rates, effects, recipes, names, and energy amounts are placeholders for the devs to refine.

Fluids

  • A new recipe in an existing machine: the RmEU produces 100B of Riftic Temporal Concentrate (RTC) ("somehow").
  • Temporal Concentrate (TC) is RTC as it exists in the overworld; 1B of TC is equivalent to 1 m³ of space.
  • The CHRONOS concentrates TC into Dense Temporal Concentrate (DTC) at a ratio of 10B TC to 1mB DTC. Only DTC leaves the machine.

Passive production

  • The core has a radius of 2 blocks, so it condenses 4/3 · π · r³ ≈ 33.5B of TC per second, rounded down to 30B/s for convenience.
  • That yields 3mB/s of DTC, produced passively for 1A of UIV. In short: 1A UIV gives 3mB of DTC.

Boosted production with RTC

  • Feeding RTC from the RmEU into the CHRONOS synthesizes additional DTC, but power consumption rises dramatically. The proposed formula is 2^(1 + x/3) − 1, where x is the number of 10B RTC increments (each worth 1mB DTC); the author gives the result in amps of UEV, with f(0) = 1A UIV as the baseline example.
  • If the energy supplied is lower than what the current operation needs, the core collapses and all progress is voided. The CHRONOS therefore sizes the current craft by the amount of DTC in the hatch, not by the energy available.

Operation

  • The core is activated with a compression seed and buffered energy, like a fusion reactor.
  • One full craft takes about 1 minute (the author suggests probably more).
  • There is no overclocking. For the future the author suggests casing- or core-tier-based overclocks, as in GTNH.

Using DTC

  • DTC can only be consumed by machines with a specific trait (for example "Time manipulation"); the author expects only a few late-game machines to have it, with the devs deciding which. Such machines may use modules to access its effects.
  • Proposed effects (the author finds the actual application hard to pick because of balance):
    1. Decreases recipe duration (the author's favorite)
    2. Applies absolute parallels
    3. Applies "core parallels" — like CPU cores, running different recipe types at once
    4. Uses less educt
    5. Produces less product
  • None of the effects scale linearly; the more DTC is used, the less each additional bucket does (1B = 0.5x multiplier, 2B = 0.25x, 3B = 0.125x, and so on). Later in the thread the author described the time reduction as roughly 1/(1 + log(x)), so it cannot be skipped through.
  • The author also proposes a custom render for the core, the lasers, and the buffer ring.

docs.title: Notes from the thread
docs.text:
• The author asked for feedback from players past ASG on whether DTC should add absolute parallels, add a little extra product (11B instead of 10B), or allow paralleling different recipes instead of changing recipe time, noting that the normal parallel and absolute parallel hatches are already very strong for late-game machines, so this must be a new mechanic.
  • One reply suggested the fluid could behave like the Hell Forge catalysts, which increase product and shorten recipe time at the same time, and did not see how the parallel options would work.
  • Another reply argued that extra product would break the game's stoichiometry (looped materials would appear from nothing), that reducing recipe time is the least game-breaking option as long as the reduction is modest, and that which machines accept the speedup must still be limited (possibly only threading multis) to protect intentionally bottlenecked lines. The author agreed that only a few late-game machines would carry the trait and that the reduction is non-linear.

docs.title: Concentrated Overthermal Reaction Engine (C.O.R.E.)
docs.text:
Submitted by: easymode (@easyymode) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UIV+ Role Processing — late-game heat chamber with a density-tuning mechanic Schematic core.nbt Original post CORE (Concentrated Overthermal Reaction Engine)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: The C.O.R.E. is a large multiblock intended to supplement or replace the pack's current thermal processing multiblocks, the Pressure Heat Chamber and the Normal Heat Chamber. The author offers two implementation options: a straightforward threaded or bulking replacement for the existing heat chambers, or a non-threaded heat chamber built around an "inner density" automation challenge that rewards precise control with faster recipes.

docs.title: Design 1 — threaded or bulking replacement
docs.text: The simplest implementation: the C.O.R.E. acts as a threaded or bulking replacement for the previous heat chambers and accesses the existing heat chamber recipes via machine mode swapping.

docs.title: Design 2 — density mechanic
docs.text:
A non-threaded heat chamber that comes with an automation challenge based on the machine's inner density value. Speed bonuses for successful density optimization are the incentive to build it.

  • Inner density is measured on a scale of 0 to 1000 Density Units (DU).
  • Every recipe has a preset optimal density, D₀ (for example, Igneferous Elixir has a D₀ of 750 DU). When a recipe is input, its D₀ becomes the machine's internal target.
  • Crafting only starts once 1 B of Prismatic Hypergurmalium has been supplied and consumed.
  • Clicking the Purge button in the controller, or inputting 100 B of Dragon Breath, resets the density to 0 DU.
  • At the end of every recipe, inner density drops by 5% of D₀.
  • Redstone variadic interfaces would display the current density band through redstone states.

Density is adjusted by feeding the machine certain materials. Rough controls move the chamber toward the target range relatively cheaply; fine controls use more expensive resources for precision and, in turn, faster recipe times.

Control Material Effect Rough Trikoductive Neutro-steel Ultradense Plate +200 DU per plate Rough Hyper Voidic Graviton Ultradense Plate -200 DU per plate Fine Primordial Residue +5 DU per 25 mB Fine Riftic Concentrate -5 DU per 25 mB

Recipe speed is multiplied according to the "density band" the machine currently sits in, determined by its distance from D₀:

Band Condition Recipe speed Very Low D < D₀ − 200 0.25× Mild D₀ − 200 ≤ D < D₀ − 25 1.0× Optimal D₀ − 25 ≤ D ≤ D₀ + 25 4× High D₀ + 25 < D ≤ D₀ + 200 1.0× Very High D > D₀ + 200 0.25×

docs.title: Open questions raised by the author
docs.text:
• Whether the C.O.R.E. should be able to process the recipes of the two existing heat chambers. Allowing it simplifies progression and reduces machine spam, but creates recipe balance issues and could confuse players at lower heat chamber tiers if, for example, D₀ is listed on every recipe's EMI page. Disallowing it preserves balance and isolates the automation challenge, but adds machine bloat and makes progression awkward.
  • One proposed solution is to restrict the density mechanic to specialty recipes in a third machine mode (for example, the unimplemented Hell Forge liquids, which could be given very long recipe times to incentivize reaching the 4× bonus). That removes tooltip and mechanic confusion while still letting the C.O.R.E. act as a final-tier heat chamber, but leaves open what bonus the non-density recipes should get; the author considers a flat % speed bonus possible but "possibly dubious".
  • Five redstone interfaces are workable, but the author suggests a specialized interface block might be nicer to automate.
  • The author also notes that heat chamber naming and use already need more differentiation, and a third one could complicate that further.

docs.title: Cyclotron and Ambient Neutron Activator (ANA)
docs.text:
Submitted by: JustObsidian (@justobsidian) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UEV (mid-UEV, both structures) Role Multi-structure family — fission-line skipping and netherline superheavy boosting Schematic ana.nbt, cyclotron.nbt Original post Cyclotron and Ambient Neutron Activator [ANA]

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A pair of mid-UEV multiblocks that work together: the Ambient Neutron Activator (ANA) irradiates Dysprosium in the Nether, and the Cyclotron consumes that Irradiated Dysprosium to transmute fissile materials into one another. Together they let a player skip certain fission lines and boost netherline superheavy production. The author describes both as optional for progression, but notes they could be made required.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• The ANA produces Irradiated Dysprosium from Liquid Dysprosium; the Cyclotron consumes Irradiated Dysprosium and returns it as Liquid Dysprosium with a slight loss, so the two form a loop.
  • Both structures are targeted at mid-UEV.
  • Per-structure mechanics are detailed in the sections below.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: The ANA converts Liquid Dysprosium into Irradiated Dysprosium. The author's reasoning: Dysprosium has a high thermal neutron capture cross-section in real life, which makes it a good neutron-capture material. The Diamane blocks in the structure represent moderators that slow neutrons down so the Dysprosium can absorb them.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• No parallels, but the ANA can be overclocked.
  • It can be boosted by depleting fuel rods inserted into it. The author suggests more expensive fuel rod types could give larger boosts or last longer.
  • Only works in the Nether.
  • Extra hatches (maintenance, variadic, etc.) should replace the Extreme Temperature Smelting Casing.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: The Cyclotron transmutes fissile materials between each other, which can be used to skip some fission lines. The author's example is Uranium 238 -> Plutonium 239, and it should also work to make materials such as Fermium. The design mirrors real cyclotrons, which use superconducting magnets above and below the chamber to direct particles from the center outward in a spiral, accelerating them until they reach an exit that leads to a target chamber.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Input and output are handled by the same inventory, represented by the HV Output Bus in the schematic. The author notes this may need a custom bus, since GT buses cannot always be both inserted into and extracted from.
  • Leaving a material in the Cyclotron for too long could turn the product into something else, or destroy it.
  • Requires a supply of Irradiated Dysprosium to run, which it converts back into Liquid Dysprosium with a slight loss. Upgrading the neutron reflectors lowers the amount of Irradiated Dysprosium needed.
  • Should also convert Atomic Nether Sludge Dust into Flerovium-Rich Re Sludge Dust, Hafnastide-Rich Sludge Dust, and Pologium-Rich Sludge Dust at a slightly higher efficiency than the normal Manifold Centrifuging recipe.
  • Does not have to be in the Nether.
  • Extra hatches should replace the Subzero Casings.

docs.text:
Submitted by: Luck (@luckytg.), Dungeon Six Potion (@dungeonsixpotion), Cry (@dzinhth0), Martin_mc (@martin_mc) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UV+ (A.B.Y.D.O.S.) / UV (progression gating) and above (E.O.H.) Role Multi-structure family — Abydos-locked resource generation through the Classic Stargate Schematic abydos.litematic, eoh.litematic Original post (A.B.Y.D.O.S. & E.O.H.) Ancient Belief Yielding Data Optimization Sanctum & Eye Of Horus

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
A pair of UV multiblocks, submitted together as the "Abydos & Stargate Revitalization Project", that are meant to replace plop-and-forget drills for the key Abydos resources with an automation challenge. The A.B.Y.D.O.S. consumes Abydos coordinate crystals as offerings and produces data; the E.O.H., locked to the Abydos dimension, takes that data plus PCB Coolant, operates the Classic Stargate and laser-drills the dimension through it, producing ores and fluids that scale with how long it has been running.

The team proposes the two structures as progression gates: resources needed for UV and later UHV progression, such as Zapolite ores and Gritty Akreyrium, would only be obtainable past certain ramping tiers of the E.O.H. (recipes that currently need Gritty Akreyrium, such as the Molden Destabilizer, could be changed to require something else). A second goal is to give the Classic Stargate a purpose after the player has reached Abydos once. The authors say they do not know what the development team has planned for the dimensional overhaul and hope the structures can be part of the Abydos content update.

An ASG variant for Nether resources was planned but dropped for time; the team said they would like to design it after the contest if the entry is picked.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• The two multiblocks form a chain: the A.B.Y.D.O.S. produces data, which is carried to the E.O.H. over optical fiber, and the E.O.H. turns it (together with PCB Coolant) into Abydos ores and fluids.
  • Both structures passively use PCB Coolant while operating.
  • Consumption rates, timers, lock durations and output quantities are all left to the development team; the numbers and resource names the authors give are explicitly arbitrary examples.
  • The team suggests the E.O.H.'s Critical Velocity mechanic could be split into separate reusable mechanics, such as [Ramping] and [Dimensional Overclock], if the development team wants to use parts of it in other multiblocks.

docs.title: Ancient Belief Yielding Data Optimization Sanctum (A.B.Y.D.O.S.)
Summary
docs.text: Target tier UV+. The A.B.Y.D.O.S. consumes Abydos coordinate crystals at random intervals and uses them to recreate, mimic and restore the faith of the ancient Abydosians. That faith grants passage to resources of Abydos that no regular drill can locate and extract, in the form of data that is passed to the E.O.H. over optical fiber.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
[Offertory]

  • In addition to the PCB Coolant it uses passively, the A.B.Y.D.O.S. must have an input bus at a specified position in the structure. That bus may hold at most one Abydos coordinate crystal at a time.
  • Inserting the first crystal activates the machine, which then operates normally.
  • After a random amount of time (intervals up to the development team), the machine demands another crystal and starts a very short timer (duration up to the development team; the author personally recommends less than 3 seconds).
  • If no crystal is inserted within that time, the machine halts completely for some time (locking duration up to the development team) before it accepts offerings again.
  • To make this automatable, the authors suggest either an item cover designed for the controller block or a Redstone Variadic Interface that emits a redstone signal when an offering is needed.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
A temple-like building on a dark base with a central stepped pyramid flanked by two tall pylons topped with crystal cages; the controller sits in the front of the pyramid. The schematic spans 24x24x25 and uses computer casings, enriched naquadah and pallaridium casings, PEEK casings, fusion coils, fusion glass, shellite glass, gold blocks, sand, a nether star block, golden idols, and a computation transmitter hatch.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Target tier UV (progression gating) and above. An Abydos-dimension-locked multiblock. When supplied with PCB Coolant and the data produced by the A.B.Y.D.O.S., the E.O.H. comprehends the data and translates it into a language the Classic Stargate can understand. The Classic Stargate is then operated to tear open space at the exact coordinates, and the E.O.H. fires a concentrated beam through it to laser-drill the area.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
[Critical Velocity]

  • A ramp-up mechanic: the machine consumes PCB Coolant and A.B.Y.D.O.S. data at increasing rates the longer it runs (rates up to the development team). As consumption rises, the machine outputs significantly higher quantities and, most importantly, higher quality of ores and fluids.
  • The team proposes using this ramp to gate important progression resources, such as Zapolite ores and Gritty Akreyrium, behind specific ramping stages.
  • Upgrading: the multiblock can be upgraded to reach ramping tiers the previous tier could not. In the screenshots, neutronium blocks stand in as a placeholder for tier 1 (the author hopes a neutronium machine casing can be used instead); tier 2 would use Ancient Runicalium casings.
  • Speed overclocking: the team also hopes for an overclock that lets the machine consume more energy, coolant and, most importantly, A.B.Y.D.O.S. data to run the highest currently available ramping recipe faster.
  • Illustrative example given by the author, with completely arbitrary numbers and resource names: the machine starts at ramp 0; as it ramps up to ramp 2 it produces various Abydos resources such as X Titanite ores; at ramp 5 (the maximum at tier 1) it produces Y Zapolite ore and 3X Titanite; upgraded to tier 2 it can reach ramp 8, producing 5Y Zapolite, 10X Titanite and Z buckets of Gritty Akreyrium.

Target tier UHV (post-RIMM) Role Utility — one-way cross-dimensional energy transfer Schematic dreeam-schematic.txt Original post Dimensional Runically Engraved Energy Access Medium [DREEAM]

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A UHV multiblock that moves energy between dimensions. Two DREEAMs linked together form a 1:1, one-way, cross-dimensional energy link that uses laser hatches, so a base can be powered regardless of the dimension it sits in. The author's motivation is that there is currently no way to move large amounts of power across dimensions other than spamming energy converters with Flux Networks.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Unlocked in UHV, after the RIMM.
  • The only hatches it accepts are laser hatches, which replace Computer Casing blocks in the structure.
  • Its role is set by the hatches used: Laser Source Hatches make it a receiver, Laser Target Hatches make it a transmitter. All hatches on one structure must be of the same orientation (all source or all target).
  • A pair is linked with a data stick, similar to how ME pattern buffers and proxies are linked.
  • The link fails if two transmitters or two receivers are connected together, and also if more than two DREEAMs are connected together.
  • Transfer is 1 to 1; the structure consumes 1% of the energy transferred to power itself.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A proposed late-game multiblock that offers a more convenient way of obtaining Draconic cells, meant to ease the grind toward the DSG and beyond. It grows the cells on a new growth medium influenced by the environment of the abyss. The convenience comes at a cost: the structure must maintain a specific internal atmosphere, it draws more power (forced overclock to UXV), and the recipe is slow, since it would essentially be duplicating Draconic cells.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Atmosphere upkeep: the chamber consumes some kind of void fluid to prime its internal atmosphere first, then consumes a smaller amount to maintain it. The author compares this to the heat mechanic of the Hell Forge or the saturation mechanic of the Abyssal Isolation Chamber.
  • Power: recipes are force-overclocked to UXV.
  • Time: the recipe is intentionally long, as it amounts to duplicating Draconic cells.
  • Threading: the author includes threading as a way to accelerate the very long recipe and to expand the machine's options.
  • Draco-peptide production (proposed): with the same idea, the machine could double as a Draco-peptid producer, based on a possibly expensive craft of a self-replicating strain.
  • The author notes they are not familiar with progression at this point and asks to be told if the design is game-breaking.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: An absolute-parallel, threading, bulking and batching Fusion Reactor built as a dragon eating its own tail. The concept comes from a developer idea channel; the author got permission to build the structure for it. It is intended as a post-DSG machine and replaces the usual energy hatches with laser inputs so that the EU cost of running many different plasmas at once through multi-threading can be covered.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Accepts an absolute parallel hatch, a threading controller, and 13 threading helices.
  • Does not accept energy hatches like a traditional Fusion Reactor; it has two laser inputs instead, to accommodate the EU cost of multi-threading many different plasmas.
  • All other threading stat points are expected to work as usual.
  • The structure counts 138 reflector casings, 543 reactor casings, and 395 fusion coils.
  • As a post-DSG structure the author expects the casings to be higher tier than the ones used; no matching casings exist yet, so the build uses what is already in the game. The author wanted to retexture them via KubeJS but could not, since the fusion coils and casings come from the core mod.

docs.text:
A serpentine dragon roughly 42x20x71 blocks (far beyond the normal 17x17x17 limit, with permission granted). The body forms a closed loop with the tail ending in the dragon's mouth; the controller sits in the central hatch column next to the ME controller (visible in the "Controller and hatches" screenshot). The glass is used to make the tail look thinner near the mouth and ideally should not be swappable. Wire NBT is not saved by the copy-paste tool, so the wires can be removed if they render badly in EMI or are incompatible with GT structures.

Submitted by: Dylan the Deltawolfy (@dylan_the_deltawolfy) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UHV Role Power generation — drone-boosted solar array that also runs at night Schematic dsrc.nbt Original post Dyson Swarm Rail Cannon (DSRC)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A solar power multiblock that builds on Star Technology's premise for solar, where valuable high-tier chip materials are spent for power instead of fuel. The DSRC multiplies the output of the solar panels it holds by consuming manufactured Dyson Swarm Drones, which the author intends to bring solar up to par with other energy sources. Unlike regular solar, it also works at night.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• The DSRC is a solar array that runs parallels, effectively multiplying its output, depending on the drone it is supplied with.
  • It has 20 solar panel slots and accepts any panel. The array stresses the panels to their limit, immediately setting their temperature to 950 K regardless of conditions.
  • The cycle is still 6 seconds. Every 6 seconds the machine consumes one Dyson Swarm Drone and launches it into interplanetary space.
  • The output of all solar panels is then multiplied by X, where X depends on the tier and complexity of the drone; more drone options are unlocked at various points of progression.
  • At UHV the author suggests X could be 8, making the array roughly equal to a slightly worse UHV solar array, with the added benefit of running at night.
  • Swarm drones should be complex to craft but come in large quantities, for example 200 per craft.
  • The machine only works with laser hatches.
  • The author notes that the numbers above can easily be subject to change.

docs.title: Fusion Reactor On Zero Energy Nodes and Crushed Riftic μonic Cold Internal Borealic Engine (FROZEN and CRμCIBLE)
docs.text:
Submitted by: 2treehouse2 (@2treehouse2_7771), 2treehouse1 (@2treehouse1) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UHV (FROZEN) and UXV (CRμCIBLE) Role Multi-structure family — two Cold Fusion Reactors that output solids Schematic frozen.nbt, crucible.nbt Original post FROZEN and CRμCIBLE(names too long to fit)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Two Cold Fusion Reactors at different tiers. Both require an input of muon-dense akreyrium to function; in exchange they output fusion products as solids instead of plasma (a recipe that would normally make a plasma makes a gas instead). The FROZEN is the UHV multiblock and the CRμCIBLE is the UXV multiblock. Some recipes are exclusive to the CRμCIBLE and require neutral riftions to create new products.

The authors say the lower-tier reactor is based on the real concept of muon-catalyzed fusion, where muons make molecules so small that they can randomly fuse.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
Shared by both reactors:

  • Each reactor tracks a muonic saturation value. If it is too low, fusion reactions do not occur; if it is too high, other side reactions occur instead.
  • Saturation is managed by inputting (or withholding) muon-dense akreyrium. Every 5 seconds the muon saturation drops by 1/4 of its current value.
  • Muonic saturation must be managed for the cold fusion reactions (the reactions available in the basic Fusion Reactor). The side-reaction products from excessive saturation are proposed as a resource-generation source, possibly for future content.
  • The inputs and outputs cannot be moved. The Futura block in the schematics marks where the controller would be placed.

docs.title: Hyperpolarizing Object Radiation Thermojunction Holder (HORTH)
docs.text:
Submitted by: IncurableDressing (@lochlan0956) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UEV Role Processing — higher-tier Fission Reactor with radiation-scaled parallels Schematic horth-structure.json Original post Hyperpolarizing Object Radiation Thermojunction Holder (HORTH)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A more powerful version of the fission reactor for UEV. Its parallel count is not fixed: a "radiation" value that builds up with throughput scales the parallels from a quarter of normal up to 4x, with a penalty if the reactor is pushed too hard.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Radiation. The HORTH tracks how many recipes it has run over a period of time (the author gives 10 minutes as an example). The more it processes in that window, the higher its radiation.
  • Parallel boost. Radiation sets the parallel multiplier: it starts at 0.25x parallels and scales up to 4x as more is processed.
  • Overload. If radiation gets too high, the HORTH voids all of its inputs. Radiation only decreases while the reactor has an empty input, so it has to be starved for a while before it will accept items again.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
An 11x11x11 cube. Each face is built as concentric rings of Extreme Temperature Smelting, Reinforced Brimstone, Noble Mixing and Atomic casings around a core of Enriched Naquadah Pipe casings, with Signalum casings on the corner edges and a Reinforced Fusion Glass block at the center of each face; the controller takes the center of one face. According to the schematic, the inside is not solid: nested shells of Auxiliary Boosted Fusion Casing Mk1 and Enriched Naquadah Pipe casings are separated by air gaps, a line of Heat Vents sheathed in Enriched Naquadah Firebox casings runs through the middle along one axis, glass lines run through along the other two, and a Heart of the Flame sits at the exact center. The author points out that the schematic shows more than the screenshots do.

docs.text:
Submitted by: Serotonintheft (@serotonintheft) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UV (both structures) Role Multi-structure family — food processing lines that boost bacteria, gcrop, and wetware Schematic ik.nbt, psv.nbt Original post Industrial Kitchen (IK) and Protein Synthesis Vat (PSV)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A pair of UV multiblocks that introduce new food processing lines. The lines output full dishes, which give large boosts to bacteria, gcrop, and wetware breeding and growth. The Industrial Kitchen (IK) handles all "kitchen" recipes, while the Protein Synthesis Vat (PSV) synthesizes meat and animal products without ranches. The author also proposes using the dishes to extend UV, by making some of them required to breed the special bacteria and cells used in wetware mainframes.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Both multiblocks have parallels, subtick, and batching.
  • Full dishes are added as inputs to new, higher-yield versions of existing recipes: the author's examples are a stem cell recipe that triples its output with a Döner Kebab, and a wetware processor recipe that quadruples its output with a Triple Layer Chocolate Cake.
  • Late game, the IK's recipes would be given as a machine mode to the FARM threading multi, and the PSV's recipes as a machine mode to the ICR.
  • The author proposes removing the miscellaneous food dishes and intermediates added by Create, the Thermal series, and Farmer's Delight while keeping their crops, and, if possible, making chickens not lay eggs. Breeding animals and milking cows would be kept, on the grounds that they cannot be automated (see the thread notes below).

docs.title: Joule-driven Unit for Industrial Coating & Electrodeposition (JUICE)
docs.text:
Submitted by: Serotonintheft (@serotonintheft) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier IV Role Processing — electroplating multiblock with consumable anodes Schematic juice.nbt Original post Joule-driven Unit for Industrial Coating & Electrodeposition (JUICE)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: An electroplating multiblock. It replaces the current recipes for Rhodium-plated Palladium items (rotor, rod, small gear, and the other intermediates) with a process that plates Rhodium onto the plain Palladium counterparts, and opens the door for many other electroplated items later in progression. While a recipe is running, the inside of the structure visually fills with liquid, similar to the chemical bath or mixer multiblocks.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Recipe replacement. All existing recipes for Rhodium-plated Palladium parts and intermediates are removed. Those parts are instead produced in the JUICE by electroplating Rhodium onto their Palladium counterparts (adding any Palladium counterparts that do not exist yet).
  • Anode holder. A new hatch, the "anode holder", represented by the rotor holder. It works like the rotor holder: it holds an anode that the multiblock wears down as it runs. An anode is made by pressing a large number of a specific ingot in a Forming Press (or, more efficiently, in a Titan Forge once unlocked). Every anode has a durability, like rotors.
  • Per recipe. The multiblock consumes electrolyte and the un-plated item (Palladium rotor, rod, etc.), outputs contaminated electrolyte and the plated item, and removes some durability from the anode. For Rhodium-plated Palladium the durability loss is calculated to keep the current 1 Rhodium : 3 Palladium ratio. The author's example: if a Rhodium anode costs 1000 Rhodium ingots, plating 30 Palladium rotors removes 4% of its durability. All consumption of the plating material goes through anode durability; the electrolyte contains neither of the two main materials.
  • Electrolyte. The "electrolyte" is an electrolyte base, a specially crafted fluid (a mix of Distilled Water, Sulfuric Acid, etc.). Most of it can be recovered by processing the contaminated electrolyte. Higher-tier electrolytes can be used for later plating materials.
  • Parallels. The JUICE can take a parallel hatch. Because a craft cannot consume more than 100% of an anode's durability, the author also proposes larger anode variants costing 10,000x and 100,000x the ingots so the multiblock can always run at maximum parallels.
  • Energy. Only 16A energy hatches and above are accepted, since electroplating takes substantial current.
  • Material matching. Each plating material gets its own anode (Rhodium anode, Duranium anode, etc.), and a recipe only runs if the input parts and the anode in the holder go together. Suggested additional plated materials: Trinium-plated Osthendah, Duranium-plated Americium 245, Chrome-plated Steel, Void-plated Zapolgium.
  • Late game. Electroplating could be added as a machine mode on the Electromagnetic Material Ripper threading multiblock; in that mode recipes would not need an anode and would consume plating ingots/nuggets directly instead.
