docs.title: Kamiokande Oscillation Engine (KOE)
docs.text:
Submitted by: Smephy (@smephy) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UEV Role Processing — neutrino flux production and alternative Neutronium synthesis Schematic koe-blocks.txt Original post Kamiokande Oscillation Engine [KOE]

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A post-Draconic, pre-Abyssal production multiblock that the author proposes integrating into the new quest line following the End dimension. It produces neutrino fluxes, which enable an alternative bulk recipe for Neutronium, and the author suggests the new neutrino fluxes could also be worked into progression elsewhere (the Abyssal circuit is given as an example). The design is directly inspired by Super-Kamiokande, the neutrino observatory in Japan.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
The KOE has a custom mechanic intended as a new automation challenge. It works like a mix of a Fusion Reactor and a Vacuum Pump: it has an energy buffer and only runs a recipe once that buffer is full.

Recipes

  • Two sets of 3 recipes: one set produces electron-neutrino, muon-neutrino and tau-neutrino; an optional second machine mode produces their antiparticle counterparts (electron-antineutrino, muon-antineutrino, tau-antineutrino).
  • Every recipe costs the same energy and takes the same time, 10 seconds.

Purity

  • Every recipe requires the KOE to be at 100% Purity.
  • Purity is gained by consuming an amount of De-Ionized Water every 5 seconds (same mechanic as Lubricant-boosted turbines); each cycle raises Purity by 20%.
  • The machine cannot run without De-Ionized Water. As soon as not enough is supplied, Purity instantly drops to 0% (like a Cleanroom when a wall is broken).
  • The water must keep being consumed every 5 seconds even while a recipe is processing. The author notes it may be easier to implement Purity like the Hell Forge's temperature, as a running De-Ionized Water recipe.

Efficiency

  • An Efficiency value from 1% to 100%, readable with the Redstone Variadic Interface.
  • Efficiency drives both the energy requirement and the output chance. At 1% Efficiency the recipe consumes 100× the energy and produces its neutrino flux with only a 1% chance.
  • Running the same recipe twice in a row lowers Efficiency by 15%. Running a different recipe raises it by 30% (capped at 100%), but switching recipes dumps the water inside the KOE, which sets Purity back to 0%.

Parallels and energy

  • When the buffer is full, the machine checks Purity (anything below 100% does nothing) and Efficiency, then runs the selected recipe with a number of Parallels that depends on Efficiency: 1× at 1% and 4096× at 100%.
  • Parallels: P = f(E) = floor(0.5 + E^(ln(4096) / ln(100)))
  • Energy consumption per run is always Pmax, the full contents of the buffer; the author recommends something around 256A UEV.
  • The minimum energy per recipe is therefore Pmax / 4096, only reached at 100% Efficiency.

Intended optimization

  • Repeating the same recipe drives the KOE down to 1% Efficiency, which is not optimal.
  • Always alternating recipes makes the KOE spend most of its time refilling Purity, which is also not optimal.
  • The player is meant to find a balance between repeated and alternating cycles, for example R1 -> R1 -> R1 -> R2 -> R2 -> R2 -> R3 -> R3 -> R3 -> repeat (the author calls this the "triple 3-recipes cycle"). With the proposed numbers (15% penalty, 30% bonus, 10 s recipe time, 20% Purity per 5 s) this beats the single-recipe, simple 3-recipe and double 3-recipe cycles; the author has not checked whether a quadruple 3-recipes cycle is better still.
  • The author warns that changing these numbers can completely change the intended mechanic (for example, repeating one recipe could become the optimal strategy).

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:

Submitted by: Joyal (@j.yal) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier ZPM (SCAC), UHV (GFWC), UIV (SCRAM) Role Multi-structure family — three tiered bulk circuit assemblers Schematic sequenced-chip-assembly-chamber.nbt, gage-freeflow-welding-complex.nbt, syntactic-circuitries-reconstructive-alignment-matrix.nbt Original post Layered Universal Circuit Machines (names below)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A family of three "layered" circuit machines that replace the Draconic Circuit Assembler's Draco Bulk Circuiter mode and spread it across the later gates: the Sequenced Chip Assembly Chamber (SCAC) at ZPM, the Gage Freeflow Welding Complex (GFWC) at UHV, and the Syntactic Circuitries: Reconstructive Alignment Matrix (SCRAM) at UIV. Each tier is restricted to one circuit tier, needs a progressively higher-tiered soldering alloy, and in return consumes less solder and (at tier 3) yields more.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
Shared by all three machines:

  • Recipes that use these machines have their inputs, outputs, and duration multiplied by 24, to accommodate the latency of layered automation.
  • Later tiers may provide additional bonuses, but require increasingly higher-tiered soldering alloy to operate.
  • All three require absolute stabilisation. Tier 2 and tier 3 additionally require cleanroom and sterile cleanroom status respectively, to keep the environment pure enough to run; this means the higher tiers carry two "maintenance" hatches. If the required status is missing, recipe outputs are reduced to tier-1 circuit(s) and soldering alloy consumption is multiplied by 4^tier.
  • Structure voids in the schematics need not strictly be air.

Per-tier restrictions and solder, as clarified by the author from the world download:

Machine Tier Circuit tier Soldering alloy Solder cost Extra SCAC 1 HV regular full — GFWC 2 IV ITLC 1/2 — SCRAM 3 ZPM naquadated 1/4 +50% yield (proposed; the author leaves the exact bonus to the devs)

docs.title: Low Temperature Pressure Chambers (Multiblock Family)
docs.text:
Submitted by: Serotonintheft (@serotonintheft), credited to Hash Browns · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier MV (SPC), IV (BALL), UHV (COLOSSUS) Role Multi-structure family — high-pressure reactors replacing Chemical Reactor recipes Schematic spc.nbt, ball.nbt, colossus.nbt Original post Low Temperature Pressure Chambers (Multiblock Family)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
A family of three high-pressure reactors, one per stage of the game, that take over several key high-pressure chemical recipes from the Chemical Reactor. All three share one recipe set and differ only in how they are powered and how much parallel processing and throughput they offer:

  • Steam Pressure Chamber (SPC) — MV, steam-powered, 8 steam parallels.
  • Bulk Atmospheric Load Laboratory (BALL) — IV, uses a parallel hatch.
  • Chamber for Overpressure Loading, Operational Stress Simulation, and Uniform Sealing (COLOSSUS) — UHV, parallel hatch plus throughput boosting and bulk processing.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Thematically these are pure pressure chambers that operate at a comparatively low temperature. They replace the Chemical Reactor for several key high-pressure recipes (Polyethylene, Acetic Acid, Nitrobenzene, etc.). As an alternative, if they should not be mandatory for progression, the author suggests they could instead run faster and much more efficient versions of those recipes.
  • The pressure system works like the vacuum reactors, but in reverse: instead of lowering pressure, the chamber raises it, and every recipe has a pressure it must reach before it starts. There are no pump hatches; the rate at which pressure rises depends on which of the three multiblocks is used.
  • Recipes are rebalanced so that only a handful of each multiblock is ever needed, to keep the performance cost low.
  • Hatches and buses can only be placed on the casings at the bottom left, at the base of the "piping".
  • If the structure unforms while a recipe is running, the multiblock explodes.
  • The author would make the interior of the sphere mandatory air blocks to prevent extreme wall-sharing.

docs.title: Mega Epic Omni Wheel (M.E.O.W)
docs.text:
Submitted by: KampfWolf (@kampfwolf) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UV Role Power generation — expensive multi-amp generator Schematic meow.nbt Original post Mega Epic Omni Wheel (M.E.O.W)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A giant wheel with a mechanical cat running inside it. The author intends it as an optional, expensive way to generate power that pays off by outputting many amps at once. It was designed with UV in mind, but the author is not attached to the tier, the name, or the exact implementation.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Input: either an existing material (the author names Minced Meat or Wetware Circuits as examples) or something new such as "catfuel"; the author leaves the choice open.
  • Output: multiple amps of power. The author did not give a figure.
  • Coil scaling (proposed): better coils should boost the output. The author's suggestion is something like coil temperature / 100 as an amp multiplier.
  • The coils should glow while the multiblock is running.
  • Hatch placement: the author is fine with either all superalloy casings being hatch-replaceable, or only the ones shown as I/O in the screenshots.
  • The fake ME Controller block in the base is the multiblock controller.
  • The author later floated two alternatives in the thread: having the wheel output Create rotational power (SU) instead of EU, and using a cat (e.g. Komaru) as a non-consumable item in an upgrade slot for a power boost, similar to oxygen boosting on a Combustion Engine, where a cat would tire and need to "recharge" before going back on the wheel.
  • The author explicitly leaves implementation details and balance to the developers and invites remodeling of the cat.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
A large vertical ring of dark casings around an inner ring of coils (the author estimates about three stacks of coil blocks), with a gray block cat standing inside and a light-blue base holding the controller and hatches. The author kept the build within a 17x17x17 box. The ring outside the cat is meant to be symmetric; the author noted a symmetry mistake to the left of the controller in the posted build (see Notes).

docs.title: Modular Ingot Processing Facility (MIPF)
docs.text:
Submitted by: Wad (@wadzio50) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier LuV (the author says it could go up to ZPM/UV if needed) Role Processing — modular EBF, ABS and Vacuum Freezer in one facility Schematic mipf.nbt Original post Modular Ingot Processing Facility [MIPF]

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A single giant multiblock that combines the Electric Blast Furnace, Alloy Blast Smelter and Vacuum Freezer, and that can be upgraded throughout the game with specialized modules as needed. It is meant to reduce the need to spam more and more smelting multiblocks to keep up with ingot demand: the facility is upgraded over time instead, at the cost of needing many different resources to keep it running at maximum speed. The author stresses that it is not strictly an upgrade over the existing blasting, alloying and chilling machines, but a stronger and more expensive answer to smelting needs, with the modularity leaving the player free to choose what to feed it.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
The facility is made of three parts that pass items between each other internally:

  • Control Station — the center of the MIPF. It takes in all resources and outputs all finished products. The controller has two modes, Blasting and Alloying, which control the Smeltery's behavior. A central monitor shows each part's module slot and the module currently inside it. The controller block goes where the ME controller block sits in the schematic.
  • Smeltery — takes the inputs from the Control Station and turns them into hot ingots or molten alloy depending on the mode. Each recipe tier requires its voltage and coils, as in a regular EBF or ABS. It does not output into a hatch; hot ingots are sent on to the Chiller.
  • Chiller — cools the Smeltery's products down for use in the factory, then sends the finished product back to the Control Station to be extracted by the player.

Each part has its own module slot. The author gives the following example modules and notes that these are only examples: many more could be made, and they did not have time to make them.

Control Station modules

  • Energy Module — provides power to the multiblock. It always consumes 16 amps of the given power.
  • Resource Insertion/Extraction Module — lets you insert items and fluids into the multiblock. Hatches can be replaced with the multi-fluid variants.
  • ME Insertion/Extraction Module — same as the previous one, but connected to your AE2 network.
  • Dual ME Insertion/Extraction Module — "self explanatory".
  • Parallel Module — runs recipes in parallel. The parallel count is set by the tier of parallel hatch used (for example, master hatches give 16 parallels). Only one of these modules can be used.

Smeltery modules

  • Blazing Module — lets the Smeltery consume liquid blaze to speed up smelting.
  • Plasma Module — lets the Smeltery consume plasma to speed up smelting; higher-temperature plasmas give more speed.
  • Nuclear Module — lets the Smeltery consume fuel rods to speed up smelting; better rods give more speed. Only one can be inserted.
  • Infernal Module — lets the Smeltery consume Hellforge fuels to speed up smelting; better fuels give more speed. Only one can be inserted.

Chiller modules

  • Improved Chilling Module — improves the Chiller's speed and coolant use.
  • Greatly Improved Chilling Module — greatly improves the Chiller's speed and coolant use.
  • Hi-Tec Chilling Module — allows PCB coolant to be used to halve recipe time in the Chiller. Only one can be inserted.

If the design were added, the author says many more modules would be needed, along with a way for players to learn how to build them; they suggest a separate menu inside the controller listing each module, its material cost and how it works.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
A large three-part complex on a single footprint: a dark, truss-framed Smeltery, a grey Control Station with a glass-topped corridor, and a Chiller block, each with an exposed slot where a module is placed. The author did not state the dimensions. The floor was originally Stress Proof Casings but was switched to Zamak Casings because of the cost for an LuV player.

docs.title: Modular Thermal Distillation Plant (MTDP)
docs.text:
Submitted by: ArcadeGamer62 (@arcadegamer62) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier Unlocked in LuV, upgradable Role Processing — modular, hot-fluid-boosted distillation plant Schematic mtdp.litematic (plus one schematic per module, see Files) Original post Modular Thermal Distillation Plant

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A distillation plant that accepts up to 6 modules, each of which can handle a different recipe. Every module consumes a hot fluid to give its recipe a speed boost and an energy reduction, and the main block must be fed a coolant whose tier depends on the modules installed. The author describes it as "essentially a boosted distillery."

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Up to 6 modules can be attached to the main block; modules come in four tiers.
  • Each module tier is driven by a different hot fluid, in order:
    • Tier 1: Extremely Hot Steam (100 B/h)
    • Tier 2: Lava (150 B/h)
    • Tier 3: Abydos Naquadite Dense Magma (200 B/h)
    • Tier 4: Americium Plasma (100 B/h)
  • Each module tier also requires a different type and level of coolant, in order:
    • Tier 1: Distilled Water (100 b/m/h)
    • Tier 2: Liquid Ice (100 B/m/h)
    • Tier 3: Liquid Helium (50 B/m/h)
    • Tier 4: Superstate Helium 3 (40 B/m/h)
  • The coolant the main block requires is determined by the highest-tier module installed.
  • Proposed bonus per module tier:
Module tier Energy requirement Efficiency Output bonus Tier 1 90% 120% — Tier 2 80% 150% — Tier 3 65% 180% +10% Tier 4 45% 200% +25%
  • The machine also contains coils. Upgrading them reduces coolant cost by 2.5% for each tier past Nichrome; Kanthal and Cupronickel instead increase coolant cost by 5% and 10% respectively.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
A large rectangular plant on a casing platform: a central main block with two chimney-like towers on top, the controller in the middle of one end wall, and two rows of module slots along the long sides. Each module is a separate tall structure in one of four casing styles, one per tier. The author did not state the dimensions.

docs.title: Neutron-conserving Atom Destabilizer (NCAD)
docs.text:
Submitted by: Lumen (@deyth), unknown user · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier Late UHV - Early UEV Role Processing — alternative Neutronium production with Hydrogen and element byproducts Schematic ncad-template.txt Original post Neutron-conserving atom destabilizer

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: An alternative way to produce Neutronium. The NCAD uses immense voltage to rip the protons and electrons away from an atom, leaving pure Neutronium; the "not-neutrons" that are stripped off are returned as byproducts. The authors pitch it as a more flexible route to Neutronium than the existing one.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Input is a pure metal dust, which acts as the precursor.
  • Yield scales with atomic mass: heavier elements give more neutrons per conversion, while lighter particles give exponentially fewer. Naquadria gives the best conversion.
  • The stripped protons and electrons have to go somewhere, so in the base operating mode the machine also produces a supply of Hydrogen. As an illustration, the authors note that converting 4 Naquadria into 1 Neutronium would produce 500 buckets of Hydrogen, assuming Naquadria is element 125 and 100% capture.
  • Lossy operating mode: material efficiency is reduced, but the "lost" neutrons recombine with protons and electrons into heavier elements. Overall this means more byproducts, more material consumed, and less energy used.
  • Possible tweaks proposed by the authors:
    • Remove the energy hatch limit.
    • Base the byproducts on a normal distribution that depends on the precursor material.
    • Change the processing type from EU/t to instant processing once the energy buffer is filled.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
Two tall halves facing each other across a gap: a pale, rounded dish built from pale casings with dark bands, and a dark cyan-trimmed casing tower whose open frame holds a cluster of superconducting coils and heat-related casings between the two. The attached template spans a 16 × 17 × 15 block region.

docs.title: Pattern Distribution Machine (PDM)
docs.text:
Submitted by: satire (@interceptor._) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier somewhere LuV or ZPM or UV Role Logistics/storage — AE2 pattern holder that spreads crafts evenly over connected machines Schematic Not provided (block list posted inline, see Structure) Original post Pattern Distribution Machine

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A multiblock that stores AE2 patterns in its own inventory and, when a pattern is requested, distributes the craft equally across every machine of the same type wired to it. The author describes it as "a better ME Pattern Buffer and its proxy, but as a multiblock" and, later in the thread, as an optional quality-of-life structure for players who already have normal AE2 automation running.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Patterns are stored inside the multiblock. In the screenshots this is done with Advanced Data Access Hatches on the front, but the author notes a different, dedicated block would be needed.
  • The PDM is connected to the main AE2 network through a Data Reception Hatch on top (ingredients come in over ME cable).
  • On the back, a Data Transmission Hatch links the PDM to machines of one type (for example Assemblers) through a new special kind of cable, or possibly an AE2 cable. The multiblock pushes ingredients to the machines over that cable and receives the products back over it.
  • When a pattern is requested, the PDM counts the connected machines and their parallel hatches, then sends the resources, together with the required Program Card, according to that calculation. The author suggests it could also display craft status, such as remaining time and power consumed.
  • To avoid rechecking the whole network on every request, the author proposes a "Recalculate Machines" button in the multiblock GUI: pressing it re-counts the connected machines and their parallel hatches so the next distribution uses the new layout. This is meant to make scaling easier (connect one wire and the machine is ready).
  • Power draw scales linearly with the number of stored patterns, proposed at about 256 EU/t per pattern, drawn only while that pattern is being requested.
  • Proposed v2 / extension: a version that behaves like a universal pattern system, exposing non-consumed items (lenses, extruder molds, and so on) to the connected machines, or a special hatch that lets each recipe set the machine mode and the needed lens or mold. The author presents this as a follow-up idea, not part of the entry.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
A small compact block of Fluix Steel Casings, Computer Casings and Advanced Computer Casings topped with Computer Heat Vents; the structure definition the author pasted in the thread spans 3 wide, 3 tall and 5 long, with a High Performance Computation Array as the controller. The posted block list requires: 12 Computer Heat Vents, 9 Fluix Steel Casings (kubejs:fluix_steel_casing), 8 Computer Casings, 6 Advanced Computer Casings, 2 Advanced Data Access Hatches, 1 Data Transmitter Hatch, 1 Data Receiver Hatch, 1 LuV Energy Input Hatch, 1 Auto Maintenance Hatch and 1 High Performance Computation Array.

docs.title: Notes from the thread
docs.text:
• Asked whether this is just an ME Pattern Buffer plus proxies with wires, the author (and others) pointed out that the difference is the equal distribution of recipes across all connected machines.
  • Niriun felt the design removes automation challenges without adding much to the pack, and noted that a machine cover for changing machine modes already exists. The author answered that it is gated to UV for that reason, like the Chemical Plants, so normal AE2 automation has to be done first, and agreed it is an optional QoL multiblock that does not majorly change anything.
  • Spiffy floated a related idea (a pattern buffer that synthesizes material patterns automatically, connected to extruders and benders over optical cable); both agreed it would be hard to implement and it was not added to this entry.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A UV multiblock dedicated to making plasma. It only produces the plasmas that can be consumed by Plasma Turbines, and it supports reflector overclocking, subtick processing, a Parallel Hatch, and a Laser Hatch. Feeding it certain fluids grants output, input, or speed bonuses.

docs.title: Mechanics

  • Supports reflector overclock, subtick, Parallel Hatch, and Laser Hatch.
  • Helium bonus: supplying 1000 B of Helium gas per hour gives +25% plasma output.
  • With Helium supplied, one of the following additional bonuses can be active (only one at a time):
    • 3200 B of liquid Iron per hour reduces the input materials by 18 mB.
    • 2400 B of liquid Nickel per hour adds 18 mB to the plasma output.
    • 18360 B of Argon gas per hour multiplies the recipe duration by 0.8.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A mass material-processing multiblock for reduction roasting reactions on dusts and ores, intended as an addition to ore processing lines. It also shares some of the Pyrolyse Oven recipes. The base structure runs 4 parallels and burns a flammable gas to operate.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Ore processing: takes a normal ore and processes it into a refined ore, leaving some byproducts; it can also take purified ores and process them into normal ore dust, again with byproducts.
  • Chemical reactions: takes dusts (some ore dusts, some rock dusts, or some chemical dusts) and runs reduction reactions on them, producing raw materials or inputs for other chemical lines.
  • Shared recipes: some Pyrolyse Oven recipes are also available in the kiln.
  • Fuel: a flammable gas is required for operation; depending on which gas is used, less of it may be needed.
  • Coil speed boost: coils one tier above the energy hatch tier give a speed boost. The author states these boosts can accumulate up to 3x, and that they only stack if the coils are 3 tiers above the current energy hatch tier.
  • Parallels: the base multiblock runs 4 parallels, which can be raised with Parallel Control Hatches or by increasing the energy tier.

Target tier LV (SAMS) and HV (GLOW) Role Multi-structure family — fuel-free steam boilers, solar and Lumium-powered Schematic sams.json, glow.json Original post SAMS (Solar Array of Mirrors for Steam) and GLOW (Giant Lumium Overheater of Water)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Two multiblocks that produce a sizable amount of steam without consuming any fuel. The steam can feed steam-powered multiblocks or be turned into power with a steam turbine.

  • Solar Array of Mirrors for Steam (SAMS) — LV, takes Water and makes steam from sunlight, so it only runs during the day.
  • Giant Lumium Overheater of Water (GLOW) — HV, takes Distilled Water and makes steam much faster, around the clock, from the glow of Lumium.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Neither structure needs a fuel source.
  • SAMS takes Water as input and outputs steam, at a rate the author suggests of about 400 mB/t during the day.
  • GLOW takes Distilled Water and produces steam much faster, around 4,000 mB/t (author's estimate). It works all the time, since it is powered by the glow from Lumium.
  • Before the GLOW can start working it has to be loaded with a large amount of graphite to capture the heat; the author suggests roughly 100 Graphene Dust.

docs.title: Stabilised Artificial Singularity Harvester (S.A.S.H.)
docs.text:
Submitted by: Kenobi (@kenobi0202) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UHV (post ASG, pre HF) Role Processing — black hole compression and high-tier material synthesis Schematic sash-template.txt Original post S.A.S.H. (Stabilised Artificial Singularity Harvester)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
A 17x17x5 ring-shaped machine that contains an artificial black hole and uses its "gravitation/compression" theme to run three categories of recipes: a TNT-free Implosion Compressor alternative, Heat Chamber and Pressure Heat Chamber recipes, and a new route to UEV/UIV progression materials (and potentially UXV materials, should the pack ever get that far) so that not every late-game material has to come from the HF.

Unlike most machines, which are balanced by recipe duration, the S.A.S.H. is balanced by exponentially increasing energy demand in exchange for high throughput: every recipe completes in exactly one cycle, and the cost is the energy needed to keep the black hole contained. The author describes it primarily as an automation challenge with "a little bit of maths": the black hole follows the real-world geometric equations of a sphere, and the player has to calculate how much matter to feed it.

The author notes that easymode (@easyymode) published a somewhat similar design earlier, but decided to publish this one anyway since the mechanics write-up was already half done, and that the focus was on designing the mechanics rather than the build itself (which they invite others to change).

docs.title: Hatches and structure rules
docs.text:
• Four location-specific hatches/buses, one at each of the four "injector" protrusions of the ring: Energy Input, Recipe Input (controller side), Recipe Output (item output), and Matter Input (items). Fixed positions avoid unwanted recipe conflicts.
  • Accepts all kinds of energy hatches, including laser (the annotated screenshot lists "regular, dreamlink or laser").
  • Maintenance hatches and Variadic interfaces can replace any Superalloy Casing. Variadics get output options for the machine's unique values (see below).
  • Cannot take parallel hatches.
  • In the submitted build the AE2 ME Controller stands in for the controller block.
  • The author imagines a render of a black hole in the center of the ring, most easily done as a 2D render that rotates to face the player, which they suggest is "somewhat accurate" to how a real black hole bends light.

docs.title: Initial startup
docs.text:
• The machine requires an initial startup before a black hole exists. The author proposes this be a time/energy sink rather than resource-intensive: for example, feeding it only 2A of UHV would make the startup take 10 hours, heavily incentivizing higher-tier (and laser) hatches. The startup would have Progress on Completion (POC).
  • Once startup completes, a black hole forms in the center with a base Schwarzschild radius, shown in the controller and exposable via Variadics.

docs.title: Radius, surface area, and volume
docs.text:
The black hole is modeled as a sphere, so radius, surface area (4πr²), and volume (4/3 πr³) are tied together:

  • Radius decreases passively by a set amount each cycle (a cycle being 1–5 seconds, left to implementation/performance considerations). As a harder alternative, the author suggests a relative reduction based on the current radius instead of an absolute one. If the radius falls below a minimum, the black hole collapses and the player must redo the initial startup.
  • Volume increases by an absolute amount for each item inserted into the Matter Input bus; all items in that bus are consumed at the start of every cycle. The author suggests the matter item be cheap (for example Cobblestone or AE2 Matter Balls), since the challenge is automation, not resource cost.
  • Containment is a constant energy cost, paid whether a recipe is running or the machine is idle, that scales with volume, so energy demand grows exponentially with radius. If the containment cost exceeds what the energy hatch can supply, the black hole implodes and the controller block is destroyed, so overfeeding matter must be avoided at all costs.

docs.title: Recipe mechanics
docs.text:
• Every recipe has a minimum and maximum surface area required to run. For additional difficulty, the author proposes voiding recipe inputs that are inserted while the surface area is outside that window.
  • When a recipe starts, the surface area is reduced by a set amount per recipe; this reduction stacks additively with each parallel. All recipes take exactly one cycle.
  • Parallels are uncapped except by the black hole itself: the machine only runs as many parallels as it can before CurrentSurfaceArea - SurfaceAreaReduction would drop to the surface area at the minimal radius (the radius right after initial startup).

docs.title: Proposed recipe categories
docs.text:
1. Implosion Compressor "skips" (low surface area, accessible and sustainable right away): a more resource-efficient Implosion Compressor that needs no TNT and outputs gems at a 1:1 dust:gem ratio instead of the Implosion Compressor's 4:3.
  2. Heat Chamber and Pressure Heat Chamber recipes (medium surface area, similar idea to easymode's design): more energy-expensive than the compressor recipes but still manageable, and attractive because everything finishes in one cycle. The author also suggests a Neutronium recipe as thematically fitting and a way to reduce fusion spam.
  3. High surface area recipes: extremely energy-expensive, and the only way to obtain certain materials used in UEV/UIV progression (or UXV if the pack develops that far). This would reduce the reliance on the HF for late-game materials and add gameplay variety.

docs.title: The automation challenge
docs.text: Because containment cost grows exponentially with volume, the player has to reach the target volume for a recipe by inserting exactly the right number of matter items, let the machine idle when there is nothing to run (to stop it from burning energy for nothing), and still keep enough matter flowing to stop the black hole from shrinking to its minimum size and collapsing, since a restart is expensive and slow. The author expects ME Replenishers plus toggle buses to be the tool for this, combined with extensive Variadic Interface integration for precise redstone logic, and additional logic to cut or enable recipe inputs if the input-voiding rule is implemented.

docs.title: Balance note
docs.text: The author stresses that recipes and their surface area requirements would need very careful balancing: the scaling energy demand can make the machine either hugely overpowered (fixed one-cycle durations with huge parallel counts) or practically impossible to run (for example by exceeding the EU/t of the highest-tier laser hatch available at that stage).

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
A hollow ring, 17x17x5, built mainly from Enriched Naquadah casings, Superalloy Casings, Atomic Casings, Neutronium Frames, and Superconducting Coils (see the block list below), with four hatch "injectors" protruding from the ring at the top, bottom, left, and right. The controller (an ME Controller placeholder in the submitted build) sits on the Recipe Input side of the ring, off-center.

docs.title: Star Breeding
docs.text:
Submitted by: White tea (@whitetriethylamine), credited together with the dev team · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UXV (whole family) Role Multi-structure family — production and processing of living stars Schematic SBB.litematic, LFF.litematic, SHPLT.litematic, SFN.litematic, SWGA.litematic, DCS.litematic, MDRI.litematic Original post Star breeding

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A family of seven UXV multiblocks that handles the production and processing of stars. A Stellar Breeding Base (SBB) locks a star seed in place and links the other modules to it: a Laser Friction Feeder (LFF) feeds the star mass, a Stellar High-Power Laser Therapy (SHPLT) speeds up its digestion, a Star Force Neutralizer (SFN) keeps it stable, a Stellar Wind Gleaning Array (SWGA) harvests its excess mass, a Disrupting Celestial Sabotager (DCS) kills a rogue star in an emergency, and a Miniature Dyson Ring Installer (MDRI) turns the star's energy into power. The author writes the descriptions as if the stars are alive, and asked for questions since they felt the mechanics were not explained fully.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
The author's General_Information.txt describes a shared star lifecycle that all modules act on.

Lifecycle

  • There are various types of star seeds. Any star seed in the base's input bus will be used.
  • A star seed starts with 500 stability. Each rank up reduces the maximum attainable stability, but this is not a hard cap, so a star can keep a previous, higher stability value.
  • Stability decays passively; higher rank stars decay faster.
  • Feeders add initial mass, which is gradually digested into normal mass.
  • Harvesters turn normal mass into byproducts.
  • If both initial mass and normal mass are 0, the star is considered dead. Harvesters collect the cores of dead stars.
  • If the base multiblock is unformed, or if the star is not dead by the time its stability reaches 0, everything in a spherical radius that reaches partway into the multiblocks is deleted.

Rank

  • Stars cannot go down in rank.
  • A star's density is based on its amount of normal mass, and its density decides its rank. Ranking up grants stability, but makes stability decay faster.
  • A star can only rank up when its initial mass is 0.
  • Passive stability decay depends on how close the density is to a certain value, which is decided by the rank.

Placeholder blocks

The schematics use stand-in blocks that the author intends to be replaced:

Block in the schematic Intended block Nyanium Turbine Casing the Mysterious Rod's blocks (from the official Dyson multiblock) Unbendable Dragonsteel Casing the Mysterious Obelisk's blocks (from the official Dyson multiblock) Auxiliary Fusion Coil MK II Auxiliary Fusion Coil MK IV Advanced Fusion Coil a higher tier of fusion coil Draconic Stargate Ring Block a new casing Pallaridium Neutronium Nyanium Firebox Casing a passthrough for the render Nyanium Pipe Casing a passthrough for the render inside the block Lanterns the color of the multiblock's render

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Creates a special space that efficiently traps and amplifies the energy of stars, then locks a star seed at its center where it can be processed.

docs.text:
• Any star seeds in the input bus will be used.
  • The controller block does not control anything important. Instead, it links and unlinks the related multiblocks, and it controls the renders and the build-helper highlights.
  • The base contains a block that accepts scripts. These scripts can activate, deactivate, or regulate the speed of the linked multiblocks.
  • The base multiblock can reduce the star's stability by itself.

docs.title: Stellar Nucleosynthesis Astrochemistry Disassembler (S.N.A.D)
docs.text:
Submitted by: rinbow (@rinbow_) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier LuV/ZPM Role Processing — targeted noble gas production from Nether Star shards Schematic snad.nbt Original post Stellar Nucleosynthesis Astrochemistry Disassembler (S.N.A.D)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A late-game processing multiblock that turns the different Nether Star shards (Earth, Ice, Lightning, Fire, and the base shard) into individual rare gases. Each recipe takes one infused shard, Refinery Gas, and a matching dust, and produces only the one gas asked for. The author pitches it as a more precise and faster way of getting a single noble gas, without the byproducts of Liquid Air distillation.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Each recipe consumes one shard, 16,000 mB of Refinery Gas (chosen for its helium content), and a dust, and outputs a single rare gas. The author describes these as base ideas that are not confirmed to be balanced and asked for feedback on them:
Gas Shard Refinery Gas Dust Output Duration Tier Argon 1 Earth Infused Shard 16,000 mB 64 Potassium Dust 1,000 mB 10 s LuV Neon 1 Fire Infused Shard 16,000 mB 64 Magnesium Dust 1,000 mB 15 s LuV Krypton 1 Lightning Infused Shard 16,000 mB 32 Caesium Fluoride Dust 2,000 mB 20 s LuV Xenon 1 Ice Infused Shard 16,000 mB 64 Crushed Ice 2,000 mB 20 s LuV Radon 1 Nether Star Shard 16,000 mB 16 Uranium 238 Dust 2,500 mB 50 s ZPM
  • The recipes are loosely based on how these gases are produced in reality, other than from Liquid Air.
  • Supports tier overclocking and parallel processing. The author is unsure what else the machine should need or have.
  • The author notes that, unlike the Exotic Gas Siphon (EGS), which costs nothing to run, this machine consumes materials for its gases, so it is not meant to replace the EGS.
  • After thread feedback, the author said they liked the idea of the shard being consumed only by chance (suggesting something like 50%) together with higher outputs, but did not post revised recipes.

docs.title: Notes from the thread
docs.text:
• Several replies considered the proposed recipes far too weak for LuV/ZPM; one suggested at least 15x the outputs, another said they would only consider using it at 8 or 16 buckets of gas per recipe, and the Refinery Gas input was called a little strange but workable.
  • Multiple people objected to spending Nether Stars on noble gases at all: the shard loop is meant to grow star production, star shortages are common, and the gases are already easy to get from Liquid Air distillation. Suggested fixes were a chance-based shard consumption, better output quantities, and possibly more useful gases.
  • One reply pointed out that because Nether Star demand varies so much over the pack, the real cost of the machine would be highly variable regardless of how the recipes are balanced.

docs.title: Synergistic Gas Turbine (SGT)
docs.text:
Submitted by: Serotonintheft (@serotonintheft) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier LuV Role Power generation — multi-fuel gas turbine with a variety bonus Schematic sgt.nbt Original post Synergistic Gas Turbine

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A gas turbine that gets a boost when it burns several fuels at the same time. It produces large amounts of power, with the tradeoff that the player has to set up production for a wider variety of fuels instead of a single one.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Burns up to 5 different combustible gases at once, using the same fuel list as the Large Gas Turbine (LGT).
  • Any gas fed into the SGT is consumed at the rate of 3 LGTs burning that gas, with all rotor holder and rotor calculations applied as normal.
  • Power output equals the LGT output of all input gases combined, multiplied by a variety multiplier:
    • 1 gas: multiplier 1.
    • Each additional gas type being burned at the same time adds 0.5.
    • Maximum multiplier 3, reached when 5 different gases are burned at once.
  • Example from the author: fed Nitrobenzene (nbz), Propane, Ethylene, Coal Gas, and Naphtha all at once, the SGT consumes the equivalent of 3 LGTs of each gas and produces the amps of 9 LGTs of each gas, or 45 LGTs in total (LGT output does not depend on which gas is used).
  • All 8 rotor holders must be the same tier and hold the same rotor for the SGT to work.
  • Accepts any number of dynamo or laser hatches, and 64A substation dynamos if the competition rules allow them.
  • All hatches and buses must be placed on Pallaridium Turbine Casings.

docs.text:
A tall, narrow tower with a wider base and crown, built from Pallaridium Turbine Casings and open frames, with 8 rotor holders; the author did not state the dimensions. The author notes the screenshots were taken with the rotor holders not yet formed.

docs.title: Temporally Insurgent Monocrystal Energizer (TIME)
docs.text:
Submitted by: Skylaar (@skylaar.) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UIV+ (Post-K.O.M.A.R.U.) Role Processing — temporally accelerated crystal growth Schematic time.nbt Original post Temporally Insurgent Monocrystal Energizer [TIME]

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
TIME is a late-game multiblock that grows advanced crystals which, under normal circumstances, would take thousands or millions of years to form. Recipes do not progress in real time; instead the player feeds measured amounts of special Temporal Accelerants into the machine to advance the recipe, while managing the Temporal Instability this causes. Hitting a recipe-specific instability window at the end of a recipe doubles the output.

The author places it at UIV+, after K.O.M.A.R.U., and notes that it can easily be moved to UXV if it does not fit thematically with the abyssal/riftic content.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
Recipes

  • TIME recipes are advanced autoclave recipes: an impure catalyst dust plus a supersaturated solution (in the form of liquid hellforge alloys) grow into a pure crystal.
  • Recipe progress is measured in units of Years (functionally similar to CWU) rather than ticks. Overclocks halve the Years required.

Temporal Lock

  • Once a recipe begins, TIME enters a Temporal Lock, a temporal vacuum separate from the outside world. In this state the only accepted inputs are Temporal Accelerants and Faematter.
  • Every 10 seconds the machine checks its inputs and consumes everything provided. If any other input is present, or if Temporal Accelerant and Faematter are provided at the same time, the recipe fails.
  • Providing Temporal Accelerant adds recipe progress in Years, scaled by the amount consumed and the accelerant's tier, but also raises Temporal Instability by the same factors.
  • Temporal Instability ranges from 0% to 100%; if it ever exceeds 100%, the recipe fails. Providing Faematter in increments of 10 B lowers instability without adding progress.

Formulas

Years = ( 4 ^ ( [Temporal Accelerant Tier] - 1 ) ) * [mB Temporal Accelerant]
Temporal Instability Increase = ( 10 ^ ( [mB Temporal Accelerant] / 1000 ) ) * ( 2 ^ ( [Temporal Accelerant Tier] - 1 ) )
Temporal Instability Decrease = ( 1 - ( 0.5 ^ [10B Faematter] ) ) * [Current Temporal Instability]

Temporal Sync

  • Every recipe has a Temporal Sync range. If the machine's Temporal Instability is within that range when the recipe ends, the output is doubled.
  • After every recipe the Temporal Lock is removed and Temporal Instability resets to 0%.

New items and fluids

  • Impure Catalysts — crafted in Mixers / Injection Mixers. They would replace the current dust outputs in applicable recipes (for example, the Aquariadic-Rimuli-Dragonix Dust recipe would instead yield Impure Aquariadic-Rimuli-Dragonix Catalyst).
  • Temporal Accelerants — three tiers. The first, Crude Chronometric Serum, is made through a complex pre-DSG processing line, ideally using Riftic fluids. The other two are post-DSG and crafted from products of black hole processing/harvesting (whatever that ends up being).

Redstone Variadic Interfacing

TIME accepts Redstone Variadic Interfaces with two interfacing options:

  • Temporal Instability % — outputs a redstone signal based on how close the Temporal Instability is to a target value.
  • Recipe Progress % — outputs a redstone signal based on how close the recipe is to completion.

Other machine notes

  • Accepts 1-2 energy hatches and up to 5 total input hatches.
  • The Amethyst Block in the center of the machine is a placeholder and should be replaced by an Omnipresent Budding Amethyst block, crafted in a Draconic Infusion Array at UXV voltage (permission granted).
  • The TIME controller is crafted in a Riftic Assembly Unit at UIV voltage, using a Large Crystallization Chamber controller scan in a Component Data Core as research, at UXV voltage.

docs.title: Thermal Cascade Furnace (TCF)
docs.text:
Submitted by: Magda (@sebo5959) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier EV Role Processing — stacked Smelter, Alloy Smelter and Arc Furnace Schematic tcf.nbt Original post Thermal Cascade Furnace (TCF)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A single tall multiblock that combines a Smelter, an Alloy Smelter and an Arc Furnace. The three functions are stacked vertically, each with its own band of coils, and the whole structure is fed through hatches placed between the coil bands.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Three processing sections stacked from top to bottom: smelting at the top, alloy smelting in the middle and the arc furnace at the bottom.
  • Three bands of coils. The middle coils must be one tier lower than the top coils, and the bottom coils must be one tier lower than the middle coils.
  • Parallel capability is based on the bottom coils.
  • Input placement follows the sections: smelter input hatches go between the top of the structure and the top coils, Alloy Smelter input busses go between the top and middle coils, and Arc Furnace inputs go between the middle and bottom coils.
  • Outputs are not fixed yet; the author would put them either below the coils of the corresponding section or at the bottom of the multiblock.

Target tier late HV (requires Titanium Pipe Casing) Role Processing — multiblock Fluid Heater usable inside a cleanroom Schematic Copy-paste string in the post (see Files) Original post Thermic Fluid Heater [TFH]

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A late-HV multiblock version of the Fluid Heater (described by the author as a "TPB fluid heater"). In Theta 2 every single-block machine in the Sterilized Growth Medium chain can already be replaced by a multiblock except the Fluid Heater, because the existing multiblock needs a muffler hatch. The Thermic Fluid Heater has no muffler, so it can be built inside a cleanroom and closes that gap.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Multiblock Fluid Heater with no muffler hatch, so it is usable in a cleanroom.
  • Takes a 16A energy hatch. Because of that, the author suggests the Sterilized Growth Medium recipe should get a much longer recipe time to incentivize actually using this machine.
  • The coils should not be replaceable or upgradeable; the author feels coil upgrades would not make sense here. The schematic uses Kanthal Coil Blocks.
  • The original design used campfires in the base to emulate steam with their smoke. After thread feedback, the author replaced them with plain Stainless Steel Casing (the schematic in the post was updated to match).

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
A tall, narrow tower: a base of Stainless Steel Firebox Casing and Clean Machine Casing, a Cleanroom Glass column showing Kanthal coils around a central Titanium Pipe Casing core, and a stepped Clean Machine Casing roof. The pasted schematic spans 5×7×5 blocks and lists 35 Clean Machine Casing, 36 Cleanroom Glass, 16 Stainless Steel Firebox Casing, 12 Kanthal Coil Block, 8 Steel Pipe Casing, 5 Titanium Pipe Casing, 1 Stainless Steel Frame, plus an HV energy input hatch, HV input hatch, HV input bus, HV output hatch and an auto maintenance hatch. The ME controller block in the schematic and screenshots only marks where the multiblock controller would go.

FrontSideTopBottomCross sectionInterior, inactive

The cross section still shows the earlier campfire base; the updated version replaces those campfires with Stainless Steel Casing.

docs.text:

• A reviewer felt the design should follow the muffler-hatch theme of the other heating multiblocks unless the point is cleanroom use; the author confirmed cleanroom use is the point. docs.title: Trace Ore Extractor (TOE) / Trace Ore Processing Plant (TOPP)
docs.text:
Submitted by: novaseer (@novaseer) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier HV (regular) / IV (parallel) Role Multi-structure family — byproduct-focused crushed ore processing Schematic toe.json, topp.json Original post Trace Ore Extractor [TOE] / Trace Ore Processing Plant [TOPP]

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: An alternative way of processing crushed ore that is essentially the opposite of the Pulverizer: the machine gives up most or all of the ore's primary product in exchange for a much better byproduct yield. It comes in two versions, a regular HV Trace Ore Extractor (TOE) and a parallel IV Trace Ore Processing Plant (TOPP).

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Takes crushed ore as input, like the Pulverizer, but produces significantly reduced or no primary product from it.
  • In return the byproduct yield is much higher than normal; the author also raises the possibility of new byproducts.
  • The author suggests the recipes might require Water, Distilled Water, or Sodium Persulfate if balance demands an additional input.
  • The HV TOE is the regular version; the IV TOPP is the parallel version. The author did not state the number of parallels.
  • In the submitted builds a diamond block stands in for the multiblock controller. Hatches can be placed on any stainless (TOE) or tungstensteel (TOPP) machine casing.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: The regular HV version, built from stainless-steel (clean) machine casings with steel firebox casings, steel pipe casings, steel gearboxes, and laminated glass. The author did not state its dimensions.

Target tier UIV+ Role Resource generation — drills and extracts fluids using Drilling Fluid and a coolant Schematic cantaloupe.json Original post Colossal Amazing Nano Technology Astronomical Legendary Ominous Underworld Puncturing Extractor.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A very late-game drilling multiblock that consumes Drilling Fluid and a coolant (Water, Distilled Water, Coolant, ...) to drill and extract fluids. The original post describes it as extracting "every fluid in the game"; in the thread the author clarified that this means the mineral fluids, not literally every fluid.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Consumes a lot of electricity, Drilling Fluid, and any coolant. The choice of coolant affects the drilling time.
  • Extracts fluids. The author notes it could potentially also cover gases, dusts, or ores, but this entry is for fluids only.
  • The output is selected with a Circuit: 0 for LV / early-game fluids, 1 for HV fluids, and so on up the tiers.
  • The author positions it as very late game and expensive to justify its power, and concedes it could still be too strong and may need a "little" nerf.

docs.text:
A tall tower of dark casings and purple frames with a drill head hanging in the hollow center and the hatches along the bottom edge; the schematic's bounding box is 17 × 17 × 17 blocks. The author did not state the dimensions in the post.

docs.title: Void Breaking Accelerator (VBA)
docs.text:
Submitted by: Serinat (@serinat) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier UHV+ (soon after reaching the End) Role Resource generation — upgradable Void resource/energy generator Schematic vba-i.nbt, vba-ii.nbt, vba-iii.nbt Original post Void Breaking Accelerator

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: An upgradable multiblock that generates resources or energy from the Void. Its main gimmick is that it is upgraded by expanding the structure itself: each upgrade is a new section built onto the base machine. The multiblock is meant to be locked into pointing downward.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Upgrades are structural: the base version (VBA I) is extended with new sections to reach VBA II and VBA III. The author's in-game explanation is that the top ring is an "initiator", an accelerator that pushes particles with initial energy into the main chamber (the vertical tube), and each new section lets more energetic particles be launched into the Void to "break" it.
  • VBA II adds a section built with Abyssal Alloy coils. The author proposes that this new section could also work as a better reflector in fusion rings (better efficiency on low-tier recipes plus new recipes).
  • VBA III adds a longer section built with AUX II coils.
  • Supports absolute parallel as well as the usual parallel controllers.
  • Power is supposed to be delivered the same way fusion rings are powered. The UEV energy hatches in the build are placeholders; the first recipes are meant to use UHV hatches.
  • The ME Controller block marks the intended position of the multiblock controller. Draconicware casings are placeholders for I/O, maintenance, and the absolute parallel block.
  • A longer explanation of the mechanics is in a separate Discord thread, which the author notes is "not really that in-depth".

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
A tall vertical tube (the main chamber) topped by a ring (the initiator), with ring-shaped sections added around the lower part of the tube for each upgrade. The base version fits in 17x17x17; the upgraded versions exceed that limit, which the author says is acceptable.

docs.title: Water Cooled Steam Solidifier (W.C.S.S)
docs.text:
Submitted by: Bkyt (@bkyt__69351) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier ULV - LV Role Steam-age processing — steam-powered Fluid Solidifier for early parts Schematic wcss.nbt Original post Water colled steam solidifier(W.C.S.S)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A steam multiblock that works as a Fluid Solidifier, limited to materials up to Steel in progression. Its purpose is to make ULV - LV tier parts more cheaply before electric machines are available.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Steam powers the machine and is used to melt the metal; water is needed to cool the molten metal back down. This is why the structure has a second steam input hatch, which is meant for water.
  • The author describes two operating modes, clarified in the thread:
    • Ingot input: needs both steam and water to work. The water is turned into steam, but at a loss.
    • Liquid metal input: takes water, the molten metal, and a cast, and outputs the solidified part plus steam.
  • The machine would keep an internal buffer for both water and steam.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
A compact steam-casing block with a narrow two-block stack on top; the controller sits in the center of the bottom front row with a hatch on each side. The author did not state the dimensions.

docs.title: Wind Turbines/Mills
docs.text:
Submitted by: enlolers (@enlolers) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier HV Role Power generation — wind-driven turbine producing power Schematic wind-turbines.json Original post Wind Turbines/Mills

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A tall wind turbine (or windmill) multiblock that generates power simply by being exposed to air, or possibly to something that produces wind, such as an Encased Fan. The author built two versions: one is a static structure, the other actually rotates.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Generates power from wind, or, as the author puts it, "just nothing" (plain exposure to air).
  • The author suggests that a wind source such as an Encased Fan could also drive it.
  • The submitted build has no energy output hatch yet; the author notes one should go somewhere on the back of the structure, on the floor layer.
  • Two variants were made: a purely decorative/static version and a moving version whose rotor turns.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
A tall two-legged tower of light-colored blocks with a four-bladed cross rotor mounted on a hub at the top; the moving variant turns the rotor on a Create Mechanical Bearing driven through shafts and a gearbox. The author did not state the dimensions; the attached template covers both versions in a region of 8 x 16 x 23 blocks.

docs.title: Wire Insulation Plant (WIP)
docs.text:
Submitted by: Kurtchekov (@kurtchekov) · Multiblock Design Contest, September 2026

Target tier LV (the author notes it can easily be moved to MV or HV if that is too early) Role Processing — high-throughput cable insulation Schematic wip.json Original post Wire Insulation Plant (WIP)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A dedicated multiblock for cable recipes. It offers higher throughput than Assemblers but handles only cabling (wire insulation) recipes, and it needs Water as an additional input for cooling. The design is modeled on how insulated cable is produced in real life (insulation extruded onto the conductor, then cooled), with changes made to fit the limitations of the game and the mod.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• Runs only the cabling recipes, at a higher throughput than an Assembler. The author gives no specific parallel count or speed figure.
  • Consumes Water as an extra input, representing the cooling stage of the real process.
  • Inspired by a real single-core insulated cable production line; the author linked this video as the reference.
  • The ME Controller in the build is a placeholder for the actual controller block.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
A long, low LV-tier machine: a base of Solid Machine Casings carrying a row of Cauldrons and a Steel Firebox Casing under a Steel Frame gantry, with cables and wires strung along the frame, a Steel Drum at one end, and the hatches, buses and placeholder controller in the bottom row. The author did not state dimensions; the schematic's bounding box is 8 × 4 × 3 blocks.

Screenshots

FrontBackGantry detail

docs.title: Files
docs.text: • wip.json — JSON template of the build (Building Gadgets format: block state list plus required-item counts, 50 blocks in total).

docs.title: Notes from the thread
docs.text:
• Several readers suggested extending the entry into a family: an IV parallel version and a late-game version, or making the multiblock mandatory above a certain tier once Assembler cabling recipes stop existing.
  • Suggested coolant mechanics: different Water types reducing recipe duration (e.g. Distilled Water −10%), or coolant fluids granting conditional parallels (4 for Water, 16 for Distilled, 64 for Purified, 256 for Acidic, 1024 for De-ionized).
  • A reader noted that GregTech multiblocks cannot specify the exact orientation/connections of wires or fluid pipes in the structure; another replied that this is something that can be added. The author did not respond to the feedback in the thread.

docs.title: Production in the Skys
docs.text:
As Star Technology is a Skyblock modpack you can/t get resources the regular way. You can't mine for ores or other required resources. You need to use more creative and convoluted methods.

There are several ways of getting ores in Star Technology, such as sieving, void extraction, fluid drilling, and generation of ores or liquids from nothing.

These methods of resource generation are covered in this section.

docs.title: How to obtain Hydrogen
docs.text:
1. Water Electrolysis

You can obtain Hydrogen and Oxygen from electrolyzing water.

2. Sodium Hydroxide Loop

You can obtain Hydrogen and Oxygen from the Sodium Hydroxide loop.

docs.title: How to obtain Nitrogen
docs.text:
1. Air centrifuging

You can obtain Oxygen and Nitrogen from centrifuging air.

2. Ender Pearl electrolysis

You can obtain Nitrogen aswell as some Beryllium and Potassium Dust as byproducts from macerating Ender Pearls into Ender Pearl Dust and electrolyzing it.

3. Saltpeter Dust electrolysis

You can obtain Oxygen and Nitrogen aswell as Potassium Dust as a byproduct from electrolyzing Saltpeter Dust.

4. Liquid Air Distillation

From HV onwards with the introduction of the Distillation Tower u can get Nitrogen aswell as some other useful gases such as Oxygen, Carbon Dioxide, Helium and Argon.

5. Exotig Gas Siphoning

After reaching Abydos through the completion of the Star Gate u get access to new Ores, from which some of them are used to make the Exotic Gas Siphon, the main Endgame Nitrogen source, completely replacing Liquid Air Distillation.

docs.title: How to obtain Oxygen
docs.text:
1. Water Electrolysis

You can obtain Hydrogen and Oxygen from electrolyzing water.

2. Air centrifuging

You can obtain Oxygen and Nitrogen from centrifuging air.

docs.title: Air Distillation
docs.text:
Guide By: Jkj3000

Air distillation is available as soon as HV, and continues into EV and IV with the use of a Distillation Tower, or DT for short.

There are 3 airs you can distill, which must be in liquid form:

  • Liquid Air Distillation
  • Liquid Nether Air Distillation
  • Liquid Ender Air Distillation

docs.title: Liquid Air
docs.text:
Liquid Air is available at HV and is the easiest one to get as air can be gathered with a gas collector. Then put into any multiblock that can do freezing recipes, such as a Vacuum Freezer, and then distilled in a DT

Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom This recipe produces:

  • Nitrogen 35B
  • Oxygen 11B
  • Carbon Dioxide 2.5B
  • Helium 1B
  • Argon 0.5B

docs.title: LIquid Nether Air
docs.text:
Liquid Nether air is available at HV with overclocking or at EV without. Nether air cannot be easily collected so you need to create it from scratch.

Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom This recipe produces:

  • Carbon Monoxide 72B
  • Coal Gas 10B
  • Hydrogen Sulfide 7.5B
  • Sulfur Dioxide 7.5B
  • Helium 3 2.5B
  • Neon 0.5B

docs.title: Liquid Ender Air
docs.text:
Liquid Ender Air is available at EV with overclocking or at IV without, but you need an IV input hatch as the recipe requires 200B to start. Ender Air is made by mixing Nether Air with End Agglormoratio.

Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom This recipe produces:

  • Nitrogen Dioxide 122B
  • Deuterium 50B
  • Helium 15B
  • Tritium 10B
  • Krypton 1B
  • Xenon 1B
  • Radon 1B

docs.title: Later Upgrades
docs.text:
When you get to parallel multiblocks (around IV), you can unlock the Large Fractionating Distillery which accepts parallel hatches, greatly speeding up the distillation.

When you reach IV and UV, you will gain access to the Arctic Chilling Unit and Bulk Blast Chiller respectively speed up freezing airs.

And when you get to Abydos (post UHV) you will unlock the Exotic Gas Syphon which allows you to skip all of these production lines all together.

docs.title: Geode Filtration
docs.text:
Guide by: Jkj3000

Rock filtration is the only way to get geodes which are used to get rarer resources such as phosphorus, certus quartz, monazite and so on.

The Rock Filtrator has two types of recipes LV and MV. The LV recipes take gravel and the MV take sand. Both of them take distilled water as the second input.

LV Geodes

Diamond + Emerald + RubyQuartzite + RealgarSapphireAll LV Geodes

MV Geodes

Apatite + Spessartine + MonaziteTopaz + Certus QuartzAll MV Geodes

These are all the gems produced:

  • LV

    • Diamond Geode
    • Emerald Geode
    • Ruby Geode
    • Quartzite Geode
    • Realgar Geode
    • Sapphire Geode
    • Green Sapphire Geode

  • MV

    • Apatite Geode
    • Spessartine Geode
    • Monazite Geode
    • Blue topaz Geode
    • Topaz Geode
    • Certus Quartz Geode

docs.title: Bulk Filtration
docs.text:
There also is an Ancient Refinement Renter recipe that allows for bulking the recipes that save tps by not including chances and giving integer amounts of items.

Bulk Filtration

LV RecipesMV Recipes

docs.title: Later Use
docs.text: These geodes that can later be macerated and put into an ore factory to get the more useful materials out of them.

docs.title: Sieving
docs.text: Guide by: Jkj3000

docs.title: Early game sieving
docs.text:
In the early game (ULV and LV) you may be primarily using Ex Nihilo to get ores and resources from sieving various loose materials, them being:

Manual Sieve

GravelSandDustCrushed BlackstoneMudDirt

Later on in LV and MV you get the Mechanical Sieve that takes energy to give a better output of ores and gems compared to manual sieving and they are GT multiblocks so they can be easily automated.

Mechanical Sieve

GravelSandDustCrushed Blackstone

Note: Any sand can be used not only red sand

docs.title: Mid-Late game Sieving
docs.text:
Later on in the game you can unlock better sieves such as the parallel Large Sieve at IV, using 75% of the inputs for the same outputs. Even later you can unlock the Ancient Refinement Center in UHV which can do the same recipes as the Large Sieve but it has access to Subtick Parallels and Bulking.

Large Sieve

GravelSandDustCrushed Blackstone
